§494 D
Poetic a)rari/skw (a)r) fit, and the intensives (867) mar-mai/rw (mar-) flash, por-fu/_rw (fur-) grow red, pam-fai/nw (fan-) shine brightly, poi-pnu/w (pnu-) puff. Also with h in dh-de/k-to greeted (Mss. dei/dekto).

§495

Iterative Imperfects and Aorists in -sko/e-.—Homer and Herodotus have iterative imperfects and aorists in -skon and -skomhn denoting a customary or repeated past action. Homer has iterative forms in the imperfect and 1 and 2 aorist active and middle. Herodotus has no iteratives in the 1 aorist and few in the 2 aorist; and only from w-verbs. Herodotus regularly and Homer usually omit the augment. -aw verbs have -aa-skon or -a-skon; -ew verbs -ee-skon, in Hom. also -e-skon. -a-skon is rare in other verbs than those in -aw. The vowel preceding the suffix is always short.
a. The suffix -sko/e- is added to the tense-stem. Imperf.: feu/ge-ske (feu/gw flee), e)/xe-skon (e)/xw have), ni_ka/-skomen (ni_ka/w conquer), goa/a-ske (goa/w bewail), kru/pta-ske (kru/ptw hide), kale/e-skon (kale/w call), zwnnu/sketo (zw/nnu_mi gird) ; 1 aor.: a)po-tre/ya-ske (a)potre/pw turn away）; 2 aor.: fu/ge-ske, sta/-ske stood.

## VERB-STEM AND PRESENT STEM

§496
From the verb-stem (or theme) the present stem is formed in several ways. All verbs are arranged in the present system according to the method of forming the present stem from the verbstem. Verbs are named according to the last letter of the verb-stem (376): 1. Vowel Verbs, 2. Liquid Verbs (including liquids and nasals), 3. Stop Verbs.

## 1. PRESENT SYSTEM

## (PRESENT AND IMPERFECT ACTIVE AND MIDDLE)

§497
The present stem is formed from the verb-stem in five different ways. There are, therefore, five classes of present stems. The verb-stem is sometimes the present stem, but usually it is strengthened in different ways. A sixth class consists of irregular verbs, the present stem of which is not connected with the stem or stems of other tenses.

## FIRST OR SIMPLE CLASS

§498
Presents of the Simple Class are formed from the verb-stem with or without the thematic vowel.

§499
(I) Presents with the thematic vowel (w-verbs). The present stem is made by adding the thematic vowel o/e- to the verb-stem, as lu/_-w, paideu/-w, pau/-w, me/n-w, pei/q-w, feu/g-w, and the denominative verbs ti_ma/-w, file/-w, basileu/-w. For the personal endings, see 463 ff. For the derivation of many of these verbs, see 522.

§500
The final vowel of the verb-stem is long in the present indicative, but either long or short in the other tense-stems, of the following verbs in -uw or -iw.
1. a. Verbs in -uw generally have u_ in Attic in the present; as lu/_w loose, du/_w go under, qu/_w sacrifice (almost always), fu/_w make grow (usually). Also in a)lu/_w, a)rtu/_w, brenqu/_omai, ghru/_omai, dakru/_w (once u^), i(dru/_w, i)sxu/_w, kattu/_w, knu/_w,, kwku/_w, kwlu/_w (usually), mhnu/_w, o)pu/_w (o)pui/w), ptu/_w, r(u/_omai, stu/_omai, tru/_w, u(/_ei; possibly in ei)lu/omai, h)mu/w, mu/w, cu/w, flu/w; e)linu/w, mhru/omai, plhqu/w (once u^), fi_tu/w. w)ru/w (u_^) is doubtful.
b. -uw has u short in a)nu/w, a)ru/w, bru/w, klu/w (but klu=qi), mequ/w, and in all verbs in -nuw.

§500. 1. D
Homer has short u in a)lu/w, a)nu/w, bru/w, du/w, e)ru/w, h)mu/w, tanu/w, fu/w, and in all denominative verbs except e)rhtu/_onto and e)pi_qu/_ousi, where u_ is metrically necessary; long u in cu/_w, ptu/_w, u(/_w; anceps in qu^/w sacrifice (u_ doubtful), qu/_w rush on, rage, lu^/w (rarely lu/_w), poipnu/w, r(u/omai. Pindar has u short in qu/w sacrifice, i)sxu/w, lu/w, manu/w, r(u/w, r(u/omai, in presents in -nuw, and in denominative verbs.
2. Hom. has i_ in the primitives pi/_omai and xri/_w; but ti^/w and ti/_w (tei/w?); -i^w in denominatives (except mh/ni_e B 769). koni/_w, o)i/_omai are from koni（s）-[iglide]w, o)i（s）-[iglide]omai.
3. Where Attic has u_, i_ in the present, and Epic u^, i^, the former are due to the influence of u_, i_ in the future and aorist.
2. Attic has i_ in primitive verbs in -iw, as pri/_w, xri/_w, xli/_w, but i^ in ti/w. Denominative verbs have i_; but e)sqi^/w.

§501
Several verbs with medial i_, u_ in the present, show i^ or i_, u^ or u_ in some other tense or tenses. Thus, qli/_bw press te/qlifa, pni/_gw choke e)pni/ghn, tri/_bw rub te/trifa e)tri/bhn, tu/_fw raise smoke e)tu/fhn, yu/_xw cool e)yu/xhn.

§502
Verb-stems having the weak grades a, i, u, show the strong grades h, ei, eu in the present; as th/k-w (ta^k-) melt, lei/pw (lip-) leave, feu/gw (fug-) flee.
a. To this class belong also lh/qw, sh/pw, te/qhpa am astonished, 2 aor. e)/tafon, a)lei/fw, (de/doika, 703), ei)/kw (e)/oika), (ei)/wqa, 563 a), e)rei/kw, e)rei/pw, pei/qw, stei/bw, stei/xw, fei/domai; e)reu/gomai, keu/qw, peu/qomai, teu/xw.

§503

Present Stems in -eo/e- for euo/e-.—The strong form eu before the thematic vowel became ev (eu) and then e (20 a, 43) in the verbs qe/w run qeu/somai, ne/w swim e)/neusa, ple/w sail e)/pleusa, pne/w breathe e)/pneusa, r(e/w flow r(eu/somai, xe/w pour ke/xuka, ke/xumai, e)xu/qhn.

§503 D
These verbs end in -euw in Aeolic (pneu/w etc.). Epic plei/w, pnei/w have ei by metrical lengthening (28 D.).

§504
(II) Presents without the thematic vowel (mi-verbs). The personal ending is added directly to the verb-stem, which is often reduplicated. The verb-stem shows different vowel grades, strong forms h, w in the singular, weak forms e (a), o in the dual and plural. Thus ti/-qh-mi, ti/-qe-men; i(/-sth-mi for si-sth-mi (= si-sta_-mi), i(/-sta-men; di/-dw-mi, di/-do-men.
a. All verbs in mi (enumerated 723 ff) belong to this class except those in -nu_mi (523 f) and -nhmi (523 g).

## SECOND OR T CLASS (VERBS IN -ptw）

§505
The present stem is formed by adding -to/e- to the verbstem, which ends in p, b, or f. The verb-stem is ascertained from the second aorist (if there is one) or from a word from the same root.

ko/ptw cut,verb-stem kop-in 2 aor. pass. e)-ko/p-hn.

bla/ptw injure,“ “ blab-“ “ “ e)-bla/b-hn.

kalu/ptw cover,“ “ kalub-“ kalu/b-h hut.

r(i/_ptw throw,“ “ r(if-, r(i_f-“ 2 aor. pass. e)-rri/f-hn.
a. a)stra/ptw lighten, xale/ptw oppress may be from -p[iglide]w (117, 507).

§506
Some of the verbs of this class add e in the present or other tenses, as r(i_pte/w throw, pekte/w comb, tu/ptw strike tuph/sw.

## THIRD OR IOTA CLASS

§507
The present stem is formed by adding -[iglide]o/e- to the verb-stem and by making the necessary euphonic changes (109-116).

## I. PRESENTS IN -zw

§508

Dental Verb-stems.—Verb-stems in d unite with [iglide] to form presents in -zw (116), as fra/zw tell (frad-[iglide]w), e)lpi/zw hope (e)lpid-), komi/zw carry (komid-h/ a carrying), o)/zw smell (o)d-mh/ odour), kaqe/zomai seat myself (e(/d-os seat).
a. sw/|zw save (for sw-izw) forms its tenses partly from the verb-stem sw-, partly from the verb-stem swi-.

§508 D
Aeolic has -sdw for -zw.

§509

Stems in g.—Some verbs in -zw are derived from stems in g preceded by a vowel; as a(rpa/zw seize for a(rpag-[iglide]w (cp. a(rpag-h/ seizure), kra/_zw cry out (2 aor. e)/kragon). See 116, other examples 623 g III.
a. ni/zw wash makes its other tenses from the verb-stem ni/b- (fut. ni/yw, cp. Hom. ni/ptomai).

§510
A few verbs with stems in gg lose one g and have presents in -zw; as kla/zw scream (klagg-h/), fut. kla/gcw; salpi/zw sound the trumpet e)sa/lpigca (also lu/zw sob, pla/zw cause to wander).

§511

r(eg[iglide]w, e)rg[iglide]w yield r(e/zw do (poetic) and e)/rdw (Ionic and poetic). See 116.

§512
Most verbs in -zw are not formed from stems in d or g, but are due to analogy. See 516, 623 g III, 866. 6.

## II. PRESENTS IN -ttw (IONIC AND LATER ATTIC -ssw, 78）

§513

Palatal Verb-stems.—Stems ending in k or x unite with [iglide] to form presents in -ttw (-ssw).
fula/ttw guard from fulak-[iglide]w (fulak-h/ guard (112)); khru/_ttw proclaim from khru_k-[iglide]w (kh=ruc, kh/ru_k-os); tara/ttw disturb from tarax-[iglide]w (tarax-h/ confusion).
a. pe/ttw cook is for pek-[iglide]w; all other tenses are made from pep-.

§514
Several verbs showing forms in g seem to unite g with [iglide] to form presents in -ttw (-ssw.) Thus a)lla/ttw change, ma/ttw knead, plh/ttw strike (with the 2 aorists passive h)lla/g-hn, e)ma/g-hn, e)plh/g-hn), pra/_ttw do (2 perf. pe/pra_ga, 571), ta/ttw arrange (ta_g-o/s commander).
a. So dra/ttomai grasp, na/ttw compress (515 b), nu/ttw push, ptu/ssw fold, sa/ttw load, su_ri/ttw pipe, sfa/ttw kill, fra/ttw fence. pra/_ttw has the late perf. pe/pra_xa.

§515
Some presents in -ttw (-ssw) are formed from stems in t, q like those from k, x.
Poet. e)re/ssw row (e)re/t-hs rower) aor. h)/resa; poet. koru/ssw arm (ko/rus ko/ruq-os helmet), imperf. e)ko/russe.
a. So also bli/ttw take honey, pa/ttw sprinkle, pti/ttw pound, and perhaps pla/ttw form; also a)fa/ssw Hdt., and poetic i(_ma/ssw, lafu/ssw, li/ssomai.
b. na/ttw compress (nag-, nad-) e)/naca, ne/nasmai and ne/nagmai. Cp. 514 a.

§516

Formations by Analogy.—a. As g + [iglide] and d + [iglide] unite to form z, none of the verbs in -ttw can be derived from -g[iglide]w or -d[iglide]w. Since the future and aorist of verbs in -zw might often seem to be derived from stems in k, x, or t, q, uncertainty arose as to these tenses: thus the future sfa/cw (sfag-sw) from Epic sfa/zw slay (sfag-[iglide]w) was confused in formation with fula/cw (fulak-sw), and a present sfa/ttw was constructed like fula/ttw. Similarly, Attic a(rpa/sw (-omai) for Epic a(rpa/cw; and so in place of (poetic) a(rmo/zw fit (a(rmod-) the form a(rmo/ttw was constructed.

§516 D
Homer has many cases of this confusion; as polemi/zw (polemid-) but polemi/cw. In Doric the c forms from -zw verbs are especially common, as xwri/zw separate, xwricw=, e)xw/rica. pai/zw sport has (late) e)/paica.

## III. LIQUID AND NASAL STEMS

§517
(I) Presents in -llw are formed from verb-stems in l, to which [iglide] is assimilated (110). Thus, a)gge/llw announce (a)ggel-[iglide]w), ste/llw send (stel-[iglide]w).

§518
(II) Presents in -ainw and -airw are formed from verb-stems in -an and -ar, the [iglide] being thrown back to unite with the vowel of the verb-stem (111). Thus, fai/nw show (fan-[iglide]w), o)nomai/nw name (o)noman-[iglide]w), xai/rw rejoice (xar-[iglide]w).
a. Many verbs add -[iglide]w to the weak form of the stem, as o)nomai/n-w for o)noman-[iglide]w from o)nomṇ-[iglide]w, cp. nomen (35 b).
b. Hom. has ku_dai/nw and ku_da/nw honour, melai/nw blacken and mela/nw grow black. o)lisqai/nw slip is late for o)lisqa/nw.
c. The ending ainw has been attached, by analogy, in qermai/nw make hot, etc. (620 III, 866.7). Likewise -u_nw (519) in poetic a)rtu/_nw prepare, parallel to a)rtu/_w (in composition), by analogy to baru/_nw weigh down, h(du/_nw sweeten.

§519
(III) Presents in -einw, -eirw, -i_nw, -i_rw, -u_nw, and -i_rw are formed from stems in en, er, i^n, i^r, u^n, u^r with [iglide]o/e- added. Here [iglide] disappears and the vowel preceding n or r is lengthened by compensation (e to ei; i to i_; u to u_). See 37 a, 111.
tei/nw stretch (ten-[iglide]w), fqei/rw destroy (fqer-), kri/_nw (krin-), oi)kti/_rw pity (oi)ktir-) generally written oi)ktei/rw, a)mu/_nw ward off (a)mun-), martu/_romai call to witness (martur-).
a. o)fei/lw (o)fel-) owe, am obliged is formed like tei/nw, fqei/rw in order to distinguish it from o)fe/llw (o)fel-) increase formed regularly. Hom. has usually Aeolic o)fe/llw in the sense of o)fei/lw. dei/rw flay (der-[iglide]w) is parallel to de/r-w (499).

§519 D
Aeolic has here -ennw, -errw, -innw, -irrw, -unnw, -urrw (37 D. 3); for ktei/nw, it has ktai/nw; cp. Doric fqai/rw for fqei/rw.

§520

Verb-stems in -au- for (a[uglide], -a*v-）.—Two verbs with verb-stems in -au have presents in -aiw from -aivw out of -av-[iglide]w (38 a) : kai/w burn (kau-, kav-), fut. kau/-sw; and klai/w weep (klau-, klav-), fut. klau/-somai. Others 624 b.
a. Attic prose often has ka/_w and kla/_w, derived from aiv before ei (ka/_eis, and, with a_ extended to the 1 person, ka/_w). Cp. 396.

§521

Addition of e.—The following verbs add e in one or more tense-stems other than the present: ba/llw throw, kaqi/zw sit, klai/w weep, o)/zw smell, o)fei/lw owe, am obliged, xai/rw rejoice.

§522

Contracted Verbs and Some Verbs in -iw, -uw.—a. Verbs in -aw, -ew, -ow, which for convenience have been treated under the first class, properly belong here, [iglide] (y) having been lost between vowels. Thus, ti_ma/w from ti_ma-[iglide]w (ti_ma_-), oi)ke/w dwell from oi)ke-[iglide]w (oi)ke- alternate stem to oi)ko-, 229 b), dhlo/w from dhlo-[iglide]w. So in denominatives, as poetic mhni/w am wroth (mhni-[iglide]w), fi_tu/_w sow (fi_tu-[iglide]w). Primitives in -i_w, -u_w are of uncertain origin. Cp. 608, 624.
N.—The rare spellings a)lui/w, qui/w, mequi/w, fui/w indicate their origin from -[iglide]w.
b. So with stems in long vowels: drw= do from dra_-[iglide]w, zw= live from zh-[iglide]w (cp. zh=qi), xrw= give oracles from xrh-[iglide]w (2 pers. xrh=|s, 394).

## FOURTH OR N CLASS

§523
The present stem of the N class is formed from the verbstem by the addition of a suffix containing n.
a. -no/e- is added: da/k-nw bite, te/m-nw cut.
So du/_nw, ka/mnw, pi/_nw, pi/tnw poet., ti/nw, fqa/nw, fqi/nw.
b. -ano/e- is added: ai)sq-a/n-omai perceive, a(mart-a/n-w err.
So au)ca/nw, blasta/nw, darqa/nw, a)pexqa/nomai, oi)da/nw, o)lisqa/nw, o)fliska/nw (526).
c. -ano/e- is added and a nasal (m, n, or g nasal) inserted in the verb-stem: la-m-b-a/n-w (lab-) take, la-n-q-a/n-w escape notice (laq-), tu-g-x-a/n-w happen (tux-).
So a(nda/nw please (a(d-), qigga/nw touch (qig-), kigxa/nw find (kix-), lagxa/nw obtain by lot (lax-), manqa/nw learn (maq-), punqa/nomai inquire (puq-).
d. -neo/e- is added: bu_-ne/-w stop up (also bu/w), i(k-ne/-o-mai come (also i(/_kw), ku-ne/-w kiss, a)mp-isx-ne/-o-mai have on, u(p-isx-ne/-o-mai promise (cp. i)/-sx-w for si-sx-w, 493 a).
e. -uno/e- is added: e)lau/nw drive for e)la-nu-w.
f. -nu (-nnu after a short vowel) is added (second class of mi-verbs, 414): dei/k-nu_-mi show (deik-, present stem deiknu_-), zeu/g-nu_-mi yoke (zeug-), o)/llu_mi destroy (for o)l-nu_mi, 77 a); kera/-nnu_-mi mix (kera-), skeda/-nnu_-mi scatter (skeda-). Others 729 ff. Some of these verbs have presents in -uw (746).
N. 1.—The forms in -nnu_mi spread from e(/nnu_mi, sbe/nnu_mi, which are derived from e(s-nu_mi, sbes-nu_mi.
N. 2.—Some verbs in -nw are formed from -nvo/e- for -n[uglide]o/e-; as Hom. ti/_nw, fqi/_nw, fqa/_nw, a)/_nomai from ti-nv-w, etc., (37 D. 1). Attic ti^/nw, etc. dropped the v.
g. -na, -nh are added (third class of mi-verbs 412); as in (poetic) da/m-nh-mi I conquer, da/m-na-men we conquer (dam-), and in ski/d-nh-mi (rare in prose for skeda/nnu_mi) scatter. The verbs of this class are chiefly poetic (Epic), and most have alternative forms in -aw. See 737.
In two further divisions there is a transition to the Iota Class.
h. -ino/e- for -n-[iglide]o/e is added: bai/nw go (ba-n-[iglide]w), kerdai/nw gain (kerda-n-[iglide]w) tetrai/nw bore (tetra-n-iw). So poetic r(ai/nw sprinkle. For the added n, cp. da/k-n-w (523 a). See 518 a.
i. -aino/e- for an-[iglide]o/e is added: o)sfrai/nomai smell (o)sfran-[iglide]omai), Hom. a)litai/nomai sin (also a)litrai/nw). See 518 a.

§524
A short vowel of the verb-stem is lengthened in the case of some verbs to form one or more of the tense-stems other than the present. Thus, lamba/nw (lab-) take lh/yomai (lhb-); da/knw (dak-) bite dh/cw (dhk-). So lagxa/nw, lanqa/nw, tugxa/nw, punqa/nomai (puq-) inquire, fut. peu/somai (peuq-).
a. zeu/gnu_mi yoke, ph/gnu_mi fasten, r(h/gnu_mi break have the strong grade in all tenses except the 2 pass. system. mei/gnu_mi mix (commonly written mi/_gnu_mi) has mi^g- only in the 2 perf. and 2 pass. systems.

§525

Addition of e and o.—a. Many verbs add e to the verb-stem to form all the tenses except present, 2 aorist, and 2 perfect; as ai)sqa/nomai, a(marta/nw, a(nda/nw, au)ca/nw, a)pexqa/nomai, blasta/nw, darqa/nw, kigxa/nw, manqa/nw, o)lisqa/nw, o)fliska/nw. One or more tenses with e added are formed by kerdai/nw, o)/llu_mi, o)sfrai/nomai, sto/rnu_mi, tugxa/nw.
b. o)/mnu_mi swear has o)mo- in all systems except the present and future, as w)/mosa, o)mw/moka, but fut. o)mou=mai from o)meomai.

## FIFTH OR INCEPTIVE CLASS (VERBS IN -skw）

§526
The present stem is formed by adding the suffix -sko/e- to the verb-stem if it ends in a vowel; -isko/e- if it ends in a consonant. Thus, a)re/-skw please, eu(r-i/skw find.
a. This class is called inceptive (or inchoative) because some of the verbs belonging to it have the sense of beginning or becoming (cp. Lat. -sco); as ghra/skw grow old. But very few verbs have this meaning.
b. In qnh/|skw die, mimnh/|skw remind, -iskw was later added to verb-stems ending in a vowel. The older forms are qnh/skw, mimnh/skw.
c. The verb-stem is often reduplicated in the present; as gi-gnw/-skw know, bi-brw/-skw eat, di-dra/_-skw run away. Poetic a)r-ar-i/skw fit, poetic a)p-af-i/skw deceive, have the form of Attic reduplication. mi/sgw may stand for mi-（m）sgw.

§526 c. D
Hom. has e)i+/skw liken for vevi/（k）-skw, also i)/skw from vi/（k）-skw, titu/（k）-skomai prepare, de-di/（k）-skomai welcome.
d. A stop consonant is dropped before -skw (99); as di-da/（k）-skw teach (cp. di-dak-to/s), a)lu/（k）-skw avoid, la/（k）-skw speak. pa/sxw suffer is for pa（q）-skw (126).
e. The present stem often shows the strong grades w (weak o) and a_ or h (weak a). See b, c. Weak grades appear in fa/skw say, bo/skw feed.
f. On the iteratives in -skw see 495.

§527
The following verbs belong to this class (poetic and Ionic forms are starred):
a. Vowel stems: a)ldh/skw* (a)ldh-), a)nabiw/skomai* (bio-), a)re/skw (a)re-), ba/skw* (ba- for bṇ-, 35 b), bibrw/skw (bro-), blw/skw* (mol-, mlo-, blo-, 130 D.), bo/skw (bo-), geneia/skw (cp. geneia/w), ghra/skw (ghra-), gignw/skw (gno-), dedi/skomai frighten, didra/_skw (dra-), h(ba/_skw (h(ba-), h)la/skw* (h)la-), qnh/|skw (qan-, qna-), qrw/|skw* (qor-, qro-), i(_a/skomai (i(_la-), kiklh/skw* (kale-, klh-), kui+/skomai* (ku-), mequ/skw (mequ-), mimnh/|skw (mna-), pipi/skw* (pi-), pipra/_skw (pra-), pinu/skw* (pinu-), pifau/skw* (fau-), titrw/skw (tro-), fa/skw (fa-), xa/skw* (xa-).
b. Consonant stems: a(li/skomai (a(l-o-), a)lu/skw* (a)luk-), a)mbli/skw (a)mbl- a)mblo-), a)mplaki/skw* (a)mplak-), a)na_li/skw (a)n-a_l-o-), a)pafi/skw* (a)p-af-), a)rari/skw* (a)r-), dedi/skomai* welcome (de-dik-) and dhdi/skomai (usually written deid-) welcome, dida/skw (didax-), e)i+/skw (e)i+k-), e)pauri/skw* (au)r-), eu(ri/skw (eu(r-e-), la/skw* (lak-), mi/sgw* (mig-), o)fliska/nw (o)fl-e-), pa/sxw (paq-), steri/skw (ster-e-), titu/skomai* (ti-tuk-), u(la/skw* (u(lak-), xrhi+/skomai* (xrh-).

§528

Addition of e and o.—steri/skw deprive (cp. ste/romai) makes all the other tense-stems from stere-; eu(ri/skw has eu(re- except in the present and 2 aorist. —a(li/skomai am captured (a(l-) adds o in other tense-stems.

## SIXTH OR MIXED CLASS

§529
This class includes some irregular verbs, one or more of whose tense-stems are quite different from others, as Eng. am, was, be, Lat. sum, fui. For the full list of forms see the List of Verbs.
1. ai(re/w (ai(re-, e(l-) take, fut. ai(rh/sw, h(/|rhka, etc., 2 aor. ei(=lon.
2. ei)=don (vid-, i)d-) saw, vidi, 2 aorist (with no present act.); 2 pf. oi)=da know (794). Middle ei)/domai (poetic). ei)=don is used as 2 aor. of o(ra/w (see below).
3. ei)=pon (ei)p-, e)r-, r(e-) spoke, 2 aor. (no pres.); fut. (e)re/w) e)rw=, perf. ei)/-rh-ka, ei)/rhmai, aor. pass. e)rrh/qhn. The stem e)r- is for ver-, seen in Lat. ver-bum. (Cp. 492.) r(e- is for vre, hence ei)/rhmai for ve-vrh-mai.
4. e)/rxomai (e)rx-, e)leuq-, e)luq-, e)lq-), go. Fut. e)leu/somai (usually poet.), 2 perf. e)lh/luqa, 2 aor. h)=lqon. The Attic future is ei)=mi shall go (774). The imperf. and the moods of the pres. other than the indic. use the forms of ei)=mi.
5. e)sqi/w (e)sq-, e)d-, fag-) eat, fut. e)/domai (541), pf. e)dh/doka, -e)dh/desmai, h)de/sqhn, 2 aor. e)/fagon.
6. o(ra/w (o(ra-, o)p-, vid-) see, fut. o)/yomai, perf. e(w/ra_ka or e(o/ra_ka, perf. mid. e(w/ra_mai or w)=mmai (w)p-mai), w)/fqhn, 2 aor. ei)=don (see 2 above).
7. pa/sxw (paq-, penq-) suffer, fut. pei/somai for penq-somai (100), 2 pf. pe/ponqa, 2 aor. e)/paqon. (See 526 d.)
8. pi/_nw (pi-, po-) drink, from pi(_-n-w (523 a), fut. pi/_omai (541), pf. pe/pwka, 2 aor. e)/pion, imp. pi=qi (466. 1, a, 687).
9. tre/xw (trex- for qrex- (125 g), dram-, drame-) run, fut. dramou=mai, pf. dedra/mhka, 2 aor. e)/dramon.
10. fe/rw (fer-, oi)-, e)nek-, by reduplication and syncope e)n-enek and e)negk-) bear; fut. oi)/sw, aor. h)/negka, perf. e)n-h/nox-a (446, 478), e)n-h/neg-mai, aor. pass. h)ne/xqhn.
11. w)ne/omai (w)ne-, pria-) buy, fut. w)nh/somai, perf. e)w/nhmai, e)wnh/qhn. For e)wnhsa/mhn the form e)pria/mhn is used.

§530
Apart from the irregularities of Class VI, some verbs may, by the formation of the verb-stem, belong to more than one class, as bai/nw (III, IV), o)sfrai/nomai (III, IV), o)fliska/nw (IV, V).

§531
Many verbs have alternative forms, often of different classes, as ku_da/nw ku_dai/nw honour, i(/_kw i/ka/_nw come, mela/n-w grow black, melai/nw (melan-[iglide]w) blacken, kla/zw (klagg-) klagg-a/n-w scream, sfa/zw sfa/ttw slay (516). Cp. also a)nu/w a)nu/tw accomplish, a)ru/w a)ru/tw draw water, Hom. e)ru/_kw, e)ru_ka/nw, e)ru_kana/w restrain. Cp. 866. 10.

## II. FUTURE SYSTEM

## (FUTURE ACTIVE AND MIDDLE)

§532
Many, if not all, future forms in s are in reality subjunctives of the first aorist. lu/_sw, paideu/sw, lei/yw, sth/sw are alike future indicative and aorist subjunctive in form. In poetry and in some dialects there is no external difference between the future indicative and the aorist subjunctive when the latter has (as often in Hom.) a short mood-sign (457 D.); e.g., Hom. bh/somen, a)mei/yetai, Ionic inscriptions poih/sei.

§533
The future stem is formed by adding the tense-suffix -so/e- (-eso/e- in liquid stems, 535) to the verb-stem: lu/_-sw, I shall (or will) loose, lu/_somai; qh/-sw from ti/-qh-mi place; dei/cw from dei/k-nu_-mi show.
a. In verbs showing strong and weak grades (476) the ending is added to the strong stem: lei/pw lei/yw, th/kw th/cw, pne/w pneu/somai (503), di/dwmi dw/sw.

§534

Vowel Verbs.—Verb-stems ending in a short vowel lengthen the vowel before the tense suffix (a to h except after e, i, r). Thus, ti_ma/w, ti_mh/sw; e)a/w, e)a/_sw; file/w, filh/sw.
a. On xra/w give oracles, xra/omai use, a)kroa/omai hear, see 487 a.
b. For verbs retaining a short final vowel, see 488.

§534 D
Doric and Aeolic always lengthen a to a_ (ti_ma/_sw).
b. In verbs with stems originally ending in -s Hom. often has ss in the future: a)nu/w a)nu/ssesqai, tele/w tele/ssw; by analogy o)/llu_mi o)le/ssw (and o)le/sw, o)lei=tai).

§535

Liquid Verbs.—Verb-stems ending in l, m, n, r, add -eso/e-; then s drops and e contracts with the following vowel.
fai/nw (fan-) show, fanw=, fanei=s from fan-e/（s）w, fan-e/（s）eis; ste/llw (stel-) send, stelou=men, stelei=te from stel-e/（s）omen, stel-e/（s）ete. See p. 128.

§535 D
These futures are often uncontracted in Homer (bale/w, ktene/eis, a)ggele/ousin); regularly in Aeolic; in Hdt. properly only when e comes before o or w.

§536

s is retained in the poetic forms ke/lsw (ke/llw land, kel-), ku/rsw (ku/_rw meet, kur-), qe/rsomai (qe/romai warm myself, qer-), o)/rsw (o)/rnu_mi rouse, o)r-). So also in the aorist. See a)rari/skw, ei)/lw, kei/rw, fqei/rw, fu/_rw in the List of Verbs.

§537

Stop Verbs.—Labial (p, b, f) and palatal (k, g, x) stops at the end of the verb-stem unite with s to form y or c. Dentals (t, d, q) are lost before s (98).
ko/p-t-w (kop-) cut, ko/yw, ko/yomai; bla/p-t-w (blab-) injure, bla/yw, bla/yomai; gra/f-w write, gra/yw, gra/yomai; ple/k-w weave, ple/cw, ple/comai; le/g-w say, le/cw, le/comai; tara/ttw (tarax-) disturb, tara/cw, tara/comai; fra/zw (frad-) say, fra/sw; pei/qw (piq-, peiq-) persuade, pei/sw, pei/somai.
a. When e or o is added to the verb-stem, it is lengthened to h or w: as bou/lomai (boul-e-) wish boulh/somai, a(li/skomai (a(l-o-) am captured a(lw/somai. So also in the first aorist and in other tenses where lengthening is regular.

§537 D
Doric has -cw from most verbs in -zw (516 D.).

§538

Attic Future.—Certain formations of the future are called Attic because they occur especially in that dialect in contrast to the later language; they occur also in Homer, Herodotus, and in other dialects.

§539
These futures usually occur when s is preceded by a^ or e and these vowels are not preceded by a syllable long by nature or position. Here s is dropped and -a/w and -e/w are contracted to -w=. When i precedes s, the ending is i-（s）e/w which contracts to -iw=.
a. kale/w call, tele/w finish drop the s of kale/sw kale/somai, tele/sw tele/somai and the resulting Attic forms are kalw= kalou=mai, telw= (telou=mai poetic).
b. e)lau/nw (e)la-) drive has Hom. e)la/w, Attic e)lw=.—kaqe/zomai (kaqed-) sit has Attic kaqedou=mai.—ma/xomai (max-e-) fight has Hom. maxe/somai (and maxh/somai), Attic maxou=mai.—o)/llu_mi (o)l-e-) destroy has Hom. o)le/sw, Attic o)lw=.

§539. b. D
For Hom. -ow for -aw, see 645.
c. All verbs in -annu_mi have futures in -a/（s）w, -w=. Thus, skeda/nnu_mi (skeda-) scatter, poet. skeda/sw, Attic skedw=. Similarly some verbs in -ennu_mi: a)mfie/nnu_mi (a)mfie-) clothe, Epic a)mfie/sw, Attic a)mfiw=; sto/rnu_mi (stor-e-) spread, late store/sw, Attic storw=.
d. A very few verbs in -azw have the contracted form. biba/zw (bibad-) cause to go usually has Attic bibw= from biba/sw. So e)cetw=men = e)ceta/somen from e)ceta/zw examine.
e. Verbs in -izw of more than two syllables drop s and insert e, thus making -i（s）e/w, -i（s）e/omai, which contract to -iw= and -iou=mai, as in the Doric future (540). So nomi/zw (nomid-) consider makes nomisew, nomi-ew, nomiw= and in like manner nomiou=mai, both inflected like poiw=, poiou=mai. So e)qiou=si, oi)kiou=ntes from e)qi/zw accustom, oi)ki/zw colonize. But sxi/zw (sxid-) split makes sxi/sw. nomiw= etc. are due to the analogy of the liquid verbs.
N.—Such forms in Attic texts as e)la/sw, tele/sw, nomi/sw, biba/sw are erroneous.

§539 D
Hom. has a)eikiw=, komiw=, kteriw=; and also tele/w, kale/w, e)la/w, a)ntio/w, damo/wsi (645), a)nu/w, e)ru/ousi, tanu/ousi. Hdt. always uses the -iw= and -iou=mai forms. Homeric futures in -ew have a liquid before e, and are analogous to the futures of liquid verbs.

§540

Doric Future.—Some verbs, which have a future middle with an active meaning, form the stem of the future middle by adding -seo/e-, and contracting -se/omai to -sou=mai. Such verbs (except ne/w, pi/_ptw) have also the regular future in -somai.
klai/w (klau-, 520) weep klausou=mai, ne/w (nu-, neu-) swim neusou=mai (doubtful), ple/w (plu-, pleu-) sail pleusou=mai, pne/w (pnu-, pneu-) breathe pneusou=mai, pi/_ptw (pet-) fall pesou=mai, punqa/nomai (puq-, peuq-) peusou=mai (once), feu/gw (fug-, feug-) feucou=mai, xe/zw (xed-) xesou=mai.
a. The inflection of the Doric future is as follows:—

lu_sw=, -sou=mailu_sou=mes, -sou/meqalu_sw=n, -sou/menos

lu_sei=s, -sh=|lu_sei=te, -sei=sqelu_sei=n, -sei=sqai

lu_sei=, -sei=tailu_sou=nti, -sou=ntai
b. These are called Doric futures because Doric usually makes all futures (active and middle) in -se/w -sw=, -se/omai -sou=mai.
c. Attic pesou=mai (Hom. pese/omai) from pi/_ptw fall comes from peteomai. Attic e)/peson is derived from 2 aor. e)/peton (Dor. and Aeol.) under the influence of pesou=mai.

§540 D
Hom. e)ssei=tai (and e)/ssetai, e)/setai, e)/stai). In Doric there are three forms: (1) -se/w (and -sw=), -se/omai (and -sou=mai); and often with eu from eo as -eu=nti, -eu=mes; (2) -si/w with i from e before o and w; (3) the Attic forms.

§541

Futures with Present Forms.—The following verbs have no future suffix, the future thus having the form of a present: e)/domai (e)d-) eat, pi/_omai (pi-) drink, xe/w (xu-) and xe/omai, pour. See 529. 5, 8.
a. These are probably old subjunctives which have retained their future meaning. In e)/domai and pi/_omai the mood-sign is short (457 D.). Hom. has be/omai or bei/omai live, dh/w find, kh/w (written kei/w) lie, e)canu/w achieve, e)ru/w draw, tanu/w strelch, and a)leu/etai avoid. ne/omai go is for nesomai.

## III. FIRST (SIGMATIC>) AORIST SYSTEM

## (FIRST AORIST ACTIVE AND MIDDLE)

§542
The first aorist stem is formed by adding the tense suffix -sa to the verb-stem: e)/-lu_-sa I loosed, lu/_sw, lu/_saimi; e)/-deica I showed, from dei/k-nu_-mi. See 666.
a. In verbs showing strong and weak grades (476), the tense-suffix is added to the strong stem: pei/qw e)/peisa, th/kw e)/thca, pne/w e)/pneusa, i(/sthmi (sta-, sth-) e)/sthsa, e)sthsa/mhn.
N.—ti/qhmi (qe-, qh-) place, di/dwmi (do-, dw-) give, i(/_hmi (e(-, h(-) send have aorists in -ka (e)/qhka, e)/dwka, h(=ka in the singular: with k rarely in the plural). See 755.

§542 D

Mixed Aorists.—Hom. has some forms of the first aorist with the thematic vowel (o/e) of the second aorist; as a)/cete, a)/cesqe (a)/gw lead), e)bh/seto, imper. bh/seo (bai/nw go), e)du/_seto (du/w set), i(=con (i(/_kw come), oi)=se, oi)/sete, oi)se/men, oi)se/menai (fe/rw bring), imper. o)/rseo rise (o)/rnu_mi rouse).

§543

Vowel Verbs.—Verb-stems ending in a vowel lengthen a short final vowel before the tense-suffix (a to h except after e, i, r). Thus, ti_ma/w e)ti/_mhsa, e)a/w ei)/a_sa (431), file/w e)fi/lhsa.
a. xe/w (xu-, xeu-, xev-) pour has the aorists e)/xea, e)xea/mhn (Epic e)/xeua, e)xeua/mhn) from e)xeusa, e)xeusamhn.

§543 a. D
Homeric h)leua/mhn and h)lea/mhn avoided, e)/kha burned (Att. e)/kausa), e)/sseua drove, also have lost s.
b. For verbs retaining a short final vowel see 488.

§543 b. D
Hom. often has original ss, as gela/w e)ge/lassa, tele/w e)te/lessa; in others by analogy, as o)/llu_mi o)/lessa, o)/mnu_mi o)/mossa, kale/w ka/lessa.

§544

Liquid Verbs.—Verb-stems ending in l, m, n, r lose s and lengthen their vowel in compensation (37): a to h (after i or r to a_), e to ei, i^ to i_, u^ to u_.
fai/nw (fan-) show, e)/fhna for e)fansa; perai/nw (peran-) finish, e)pe/ra_na for e)peransa; ste/llw (stel-) send, e)/steila for e)stelsa; kri/_nw (krin-) judge, e)/kri_na for e)krinsa; a(/llomai (a(l-) leap, h(la/mhn for h(lsamhn.
a. Some verbs in -ainw (-an-) have -a_na instead of -hna; as glukai/nw sweeten e)glu/ka_na. So i)sxnai/nw make thin, kerdai/nw gain, koilai/nw hollow out, lipai/nw fatten, o)rgai/nw be angry, pepai/nw make ripe. Cp. 30 a.
b. The poetic verbs retaining s in the future (536) retain it also in the aorist.
c. ai)/rw (a)r-) raise is treated as if its verb-stem were a)_r- (contracted from a)er- in a)ei/rw): aor. h)=ra, a)/_rw, a)/_raimi, a)=ron, a)=rai, a)/_ras, and h)ra/mhn, a)/_rwmai, a)_rai/mhn, a)/_rasqai, a)_ra/menos.
d. h)/negka is used as the first aorist of fe/rw bear. ei)=pa is rare for ei)=pon (549).

§544 D
Hom. has Ionic -hna for -a_na after i or r. Aeolic assimilates s to a liquid; as e)/krinna, a)pe/stella, e)ne/mmato, sune/rraisa (= sunei/ra_sa). Cp. Hom. w)/felle (o)fe/llw increase).

§545

Stop Verbs.—Labial (p, b, f) and palatal (k, g, x) stops at the end of the verb-stem unite with s to form y or c. Dentals (t, d, q) are lost before s (cp. 98).
pe/mp-w send e)/pemya, e)pemya/mhn; bla/ptw (blab-) injure e)/blaya; gra/f-w write e)/graya, e)graya/mhn; ple/k-w weave e)/pleca, e)pleca/mhn; le/g-w say e)/leca; tara/ttw (tarax-) disturb e)ta/raca, e)taraca/mhn; poetic e)re/ssw (e)ret-) row h)/resa; fra/zw (frad-) tell e)/frasa, e)frasa/mhn; pei/q-w (piq-, peiq-, poiq-) persuade e)/peisa.
a. On forms in s from stems in g see 516.

§545 D
Hom. often has ss from dental stems, as e)ko/missa e)komissa/mhn (komi/zw). Doric has -ca from most verbs in -zw; Hom. also has c (h(/rpace). See 516 D.

## IV. SECOND AORIST SYSTEM

## (SECOND AORIST ACTIVE AND MIDDLE)

§546
The second aorist is formed without any tense-suffix and only from the simple verb-stem. Only primitive verbs (372) have second aorists.

§546 D
Hom. has more second aorists than Attic, which favoured the first aorist. Some derivative verbs have Homeric second aorists classed under them for convenience only, as ktupe/w sound e)/ktupon; mu_ka/omai roar e)/mukon; stuge/w hate e)/stugon. These forms are derived from the pure verb-stem (485 d, 553).

§547
(I) *w-Verbs.—*w-verbs make the second aorist by adding o/e- to the verb-stem, which regularly ends in a consonant. Verbs showing vowel gradations (476) use the weak stem (otherwise there would be confusion with the imperfect).
lei/pw (lip-, leip-) leave e)/lipon, -e)lipo/mhn; feu/gw (fug-, feug-) flee e)/fugon; pe/tomai fly e)pto/mhn (476 a); lamba/nw (lab-) take e)/labon.

§547 D
Hom. often has no thematic vowel in the middle voice of w-verbs (e)de/gmhn from de/xomai receive). See 634. 688.

§548

a. Vowel verbs rarely form second aorists, as the irregular ai)re/w seize (ei)=lon, 529. 1), e)sqi/w eat (e)/fagon), o(ra/w (ei)=don). e)/pion drank (pi/_nw) is the only second aorist in prose from a vowel stem and having thematic inflection.
b. Many w-verbs with stems ending in a vowel have second aorists formed like those of mi-verbs. These are enumerated in 687.

§549
Verbs of the First Class (499) adding a thematic vowel to the verbstem form the second aorist (1) by reduplication (494), as a)/gw lead h)/gagon, and ei)=pon probably for e)-ve-vep-on; (2) by syncope (493), as pe/tomai fly e)pto/mhn, e)gei/rw (e)ger-) rouse h)gro/mhn, e(/pomai (sep-) jollow e)spo/mhn, imperf. ei/po/mhn from e)-sepomhn, e)/xw (sex-) hare e)/sxon; (3) by using a for e (476 b) in poetic forms (480), as tre/pw turn e)/trapon; (4) by metathesis (492), as poet. de/rkomai see e)/drakon.

§549 D
(1) Hom. has (e'）ke/kleto (ke/lo-mai command), le/laqon (lh/q-w lie hid), e)pe/frade (fra/zw tell), pepiqei=n (pei/q-w persuade). h)ru/_kakon (e)ru/_k-w check), h)ni/_papon and e)ne/ni_pon (e)ni/ptw chide, e)nip-) have unusual formation. (2) e)-pl-o/mhn (pe/lo-mai am, come, pel-). (3) e)/praqon (pe/rq-w sack), e)/tamon (te/m-n-w cut). (4) blh=to (ba/llw hit, 128 a).

§550
(II) *mi-Verbs.—The stem of the second aorist of mi-verbs is the verb-stem without any thematic vowel. In the indicative active the strong form of the stem, which ends in a vowel, is regularly employed. The middle uses the weak stem form.
i(/-sth-mi (sta-, sth-) set, second aorist e)/sthn, e)/sths, e)/sth, e)/sthton, e)sth/thn, e)/sthmen, e)/sthte, e)/sthsan; middle e)-qe/-mhn from ti/qhmi (qe-, qh-) place, e)-do/-mhn from di/dwmi (do-, dw-) give.

§551
Originally only the dual and plural showed the weak forms, which are retained in the second aorists of ti/qhmi, di/dwmi, and i(/_hmi: e)/qemen, e)/domen, ei(=men (e)-e/men), and in Hom. ba/thn (also bh/thn) from e)/bhn went. Elsewhere the weak grades have been displaced by the strong grades, which forced their way in from the singular. Thus, e)/gnon, e)/fu^n in Pindar (= e)/gnw-san, e)/fu_-san), which come from e)gnwn（t), e)fu_n（t) by 40. So Hom. e)/tla^n, e)/ba^n. Such 3 pl. forms are rare in the dramatic poets.
a. For the singular of ti/qhmi, di/dwmi, i(/_hmi, see 755; for the imperatives, 759; for the infinitives, 760.

§551 D
Hom. has e)/kta^n I slew (ktei/nw, kten-) with a^ taken from e)/kta^men, and ou)=ta he wounded (ou)ta/w).

§552
No verb in -u_mi has a second aorist in Attic from the stem in u.

§553
The difference between an imperfect and an aorist depends formally on the character of the present. Thus e)/-fh-n said is called an ‘imperfect’ of fh-mi/: but e)/-sth-n stood is a ‘second aorist’ because it shows a different tense-stem than that of i(/sthmi. Similarly e)/-fer-on is ‘imperfect’ to fe/rw, but e)/-tek-on ‘second aorist’ to ti/ktw because there is no present tekw. e)/stixon is imperfect to sti/xw, but second aorist to stei/xw. Cp. 546 D.

## NOTE ON THE SECOND AORIST AND SECOND PERFECT

§554

a. The second aorist and the second perfect are usually formed only from primitive verbs (372). These tenses are formed by adding the personal endings (inclusive of the thematic or tense vowel) to the verb-stem without any consonant tense-suffix. Cp. e)/lipo-n with e)/lu_-s-a, e)tra/p-hn with e)tre/f-q-hn (tre/pw turn), ge/-graf-a with le/lu-k-a.
b. The second perfect and second aorist passive are historically older than the corresponding first perfect and first aorist.
c. tre/pw turn is the only verb that has three first aorists and three second aorists (596).
d. Very few verbs have both the second aorist active and the second aorist passive. In cases where both occur, one form is rare, as e)/tupon (once in poetry), e)tu/phn (tu/ptw strike).
e. In the same voice both the first and the second aorist (or perfect) are rare, as e)/fqasa, e)/fqhn (fqa/nw anticipate). When both occur, the first aorist (or perfect) is often transitive, the second aorist (or perfect) is intransitive (819); as e)/sthsa I erected, i.e. made stand, e)/sthn I stood. In other cases one aorist is used in prose, the other in poetry: e)/peisa, poet. e)/piqon (pei/qw persuade); or they occur in different dialects, as Attic e)ta/fhn, Ionic e)qa/fqhn (qa/ptw bury); or one is much later than the other, as e)/leiya, late for e)/lipon.

## V. FIRST (K) PERFECT SYSTEM

## (FIRST PERFECT AND PLUPERFECT ACTIVE)

§555
The stem of the first perfect is formed by adding -ka to the reduplicated verb-stem. le/-lu-ka I have loosed, e)-le-lu/kh I had loosed.
a. The k-perfect is later in origin than the second perfect and seems to have started from verb-stems in -k, as e)/-oik-a (= ve/-voik-a) from ei)/kw resemble.
b. Verbs showing the gradations ei, eu: oi, ou: i, u (476) have ei, eu; as pei/qw (piq-, peiq-) persuade pe/peika (560). But de/doika fear has oi (cp. 564).

§555 b. D
Hom. dei/dw (used as a present) is for de-dvo ([iglide]）-a. deid- was written on account of the metre when v was lost. Hom. de/dia is for de-d（v）i-a with the weak root that is used in de/dimen. See 703 D.

§556
The first perfect is formed from verb-stems ending in a vowel, a liquid, or a dental stop (t, d, q).

§557

Vowel Verbs.—Vowel verbs lengthen the final vowel (if short) before -ka, as ti_ma/-w honour te-ti/_mh-ka, e)a/-w permit ei)/a_-ka, poie/-w make pe-poi/h-ka, ti/qhmi (qe-, qh-) place te/-qh-ka, di/dwmi (do-, dw-) give de/-dw-ka.

§557 D
1. Hom. has the k-perfect only in verbs with vowel verb-stems. Of these some have the second perfect in -a, particularly in participles. Thus kekmhw/s, Attic kekmhkw/s (ka/m-n-w am weary); kekorhw/s (kore/-nnu_mi satiate); pefu/_ka_si and pefu/a_si (fu/w produce).
2. In some dialects a present was derived from the perfect stem; as Hom. a)nw/gw, Theocr. dedoi/kw, pefu/_kei (in the 2 perf.: Theocr. pepo/nqw). Inf. teqna/khn (Aeol.), part. keklh/gontes (Hom.), pefri/_kwn (Pind.).
3. From me/mhka (mhka/omai bleat) Hom. has the plup. e)me/mhkon.

§558
This applies to verbs that add e (485). For verbs that retain a short final vowel, see 488. (Except sbe/nnu_mi (sbe-) extinguish, which has e)/sbhka.)

§559

Liquid Verbs.—Many liquid verbs have no perfect or employ the second perfect. Examples of the regular formation are fai/nw (fan-) show, pe/fagka, a)gge/llw (a)ggel-) announce, h)/ggelka.
a. Some liquid verbs drop n; as ke/krika, ke/klika from kri/_nw (krin-) judge, kli/_nw (klin-) incline. tei/nw (ten-) stretch has te/taka from tetṇka.
b. Monosyllabic stems change e to a; as e)/stalka, e)/fqarka from ste/llw (stel-) send, fqei/rw (fqer-) corrupt.
N. For a we expect o; a is derived from the middle (e)/stalmai, e)/fqarmai).
c. All stems in m and many others add e (485); as ne/mw (nem-e-), distribute nene/mhka, me/lw (mel-e-) care for meme/lhka, tugxa/nw (tux-e) happen tetu/xhka.
d. Many liquid verbs suffer metathesis (492) and thus get the form of vowel verbs; as ba/llw (bal-) throw be/blhka; qnh/|skw (qan-) die te/qnhka; kale/w (kale-, klh-) call ke/klhka; ka/mnw (kam-) am weary ke/kmhka; te/mnw (tem-) cut te/tmhka. Also pi/_ptw (pet-, pto-) fall pe/ptwka. See 128 a.

§560

Stop Verbs.—Dental stems drop t, d, q before -ka; as pei/qw (piq-, peiq-, poiq-) persuade pe/peika, komi/zw (komid-) carry keko/mika.

## VI. SECOND PERFECT SYSTEM

## (SECOND PERFECT AND PLUPERFECT ACTIVE)

§561
The stem of the second perfect is formed by adding a to the reduplicated verb-stem: ge/-graf-a I have written (gra/f-w).

§561 D
Hom. has several forms unknown to Attic: de/doupa (doup-e/-w sound), e)/olpa (e)/lp-w hope), e)/orga (r(e/zw work), pro-be/boula (bou/lomai wish), me/mhla (me/lw care for).

§562
The second perfect is almost always formed from stems ending in a liquid or a stop consonant, and not from vowel stems.
a. a)kh/koa (a)kou/w hear) is for a)khko（v）-a (a)kov- = a)ko[uglide]-, 43).

§562 D
But de/dia fear from dvi-. See 555 b. D., 703.

§563
Verb-stems showing variation between short and long vowels (476) have long vowels in the second perfect (a^ is thus regularly lengthened). Thus, th/kw (tak-, thk-) melt te/thka, kra/_zw (krag-) cry out ke/kra_ga, fai/nw (fan-) show pe/fhna have appeared (but pe/fagka have shown), r(h/gnu_mi (r(ag-, r(hg-, r(wg-, 477 c) break e)/rrwga.
a. ei)/wqa am accustomed ( = se-svwq-a) has the strong form w (cp. h)=qos custom, 123); Hom. e)/qw (Attic e)qi/zw accustom).

§564
The second perfect has o, oi when the verb-stem varies between a, e, o (478, 479) or i, ei, oi (477 a): tre/f-w (tref-, trof-, traf-) nourish te/trofa, lei/pw (lip-, leip-, loip-) leave le/loipa, pei/qw (piq-, peiq-, poiq-) persuade pe/poiqa trust.

§565
Similarly verbs with the variation u, eu, ou (476) should have ou; but this occurs only in Epic ei)lh/louqa ( = Att. e)lh/luqa); cp. e)leu/（q）-somai. Other verbs have eu, as feu/gw flee pe/feuga.

§566
After Attic reduplication (446) the stem of the second perfect has the weak form; a)lei/fw (a)leif-, a)lif-) anoint a)lh/lifa.

§567
Apart from the variations in 563-566 the vowel of the verb-stem remains unchanged: as ge/grafa (gra/fw write), ke/ku_fa (ku/_ptw stoop, ku_f-).

§568
The meaning of the second perfect may differ from that of the present; as e)grh/gora am awake from e)gei/rw wake up, se/shra grin from sai/rw sweep. The second perfect often has the force of a present; as pe/poiqa trust (pe/peika have persuaded). See 819.

§569

Aspirated Second Perfects.—In many stems a final p or b changes to f: a final k or g changes to x. (f and x here imitate verb-stems in f and x, as tre/fw, o)ru/ttw.)
ko/ptw (kop-) cut ke/kofa, pe/mp-w send pe/pomfa, bla/ptw (blab-) injure be/blafa, tri/_bw (tri_b-) rub te/tri^fa, fula/ttw (fulak-) guard -pefu/laxa; tre/f-w (tref-) nourish te/trofa; o)ru/ttw (o)rux-) dig o)rw/ruxa.

§569 D
Hom. never aspirates p, b, k, g. Thus kekopw/s = Att. kekofw/s (ko/p-t-w cut). The aspirated perfect occurs once in Hdt. (e)pepo/mfei 1. 85); but is unknown in Attic until the fifth century B.C. Soph. Tr. 1009 (a)nate/trofas) is the only example in tragedy.

§570
Most such stems have a short vowel immediately before the final consonant; a long vowel precedes e.g. in dei/k-nu_-mi de/deixa, khru/_ttw (khru_k-) -kekhru_xa, pth/ssw (pthk-) e)/pthxa. te/trifa and te/qlifa show i^ in contrast to i_ in the present (tri/_bw, qli/_bw). ste/rgw, la/mpw do not aspirate (e)/storga, poet. le/lampa).

§571
The following verbs have aspirated second perfects: a)/gw, a)lla/ttw, a)noi/gw, bla/ptw, dei/knu_mi, diw/kw (rare), qli/_bw, khru/_ttw, kle/ptw, ko/ptw, lagxa/nw, lamba/nw, la/ptw, le/gw collect, ma/ttw, mei/gnu_mi, pe/mpw, ple/kw, pra/_ttw, pth/ssw, ta/ttw, tre/pw, tri/_bw, fe/rw (e)nh/noxa), fula/ttw. a)noi/gw or a)noi/gnu_mi has two perfects: a)ne/w|xa and a)ne/w|ga. pra/_ttw do has pe/pra_ga have done and fare (well or ill), and (generally later) pe/pra_xa have done.

§572

Second Perfects of the mi-form.—Some verbs add the endings directly to the reduplicated verb-stem. Such second perfects lack the singular of the indicative.
i(/sthmi (sta-, sth-) set, 2 perf. stem e(sta-: e(/sta-men, e(/sta-te, e(sta=si, inf. e(sta/-nai; 2 plup. e(/sta-san (417). The singular is supplied by the forms in -ka; as e(/sthka. These second perfects are enumerated in 704.

§573

Stem Gradation.—Originally the second perfect was inflected throughout without any thematic vowel (cp. the perfect middle), but with stem-gradation: strong forms in the singular, weak forms elsewhere. -a (1 singular) was introduced in part from the aorist and spread to the other persons. Corresponding to the inflection of oi)=da (794) we expect pe/poiqa, pe/poisqa, pe/poiqe, pe/piston, pe/piqmen, pe/piste, pepi/qati (from pepiqṇti). Traces of this mode of inflection appear in Hom. gega/thn (from gegṇthn, 35 b) ge/gamen from ge/gona; e)/i+kton, e)i+/kthn, e)i+kw/s from e)/oika; e)pe/piqmen; me/mamen from me/mona; pe/pasqe (for pepaqte = pepṇqte) from pe/ponqa (other examples 704, 705). So the masc. and neut. participles have the strong forms, the feminine has the weak forms (memhkw/s, memakui=a as ei)dw/s, i)dui=a).

## VII. PERFECT MIDDLE SYSTEM

## (PERFECT AND PLUPERFECT MIDDLE AND PASSIVE, FUTURE PERFECT PASSIVE)

§574
The stem of the perfect and pluperfect middle and passive is the reduplicated verb-stem, to which the personal endings are directly attached. le/lu-mai I have loosed myself or have been loosed, e)-lelu/-mhn; de/do-mai (di/-dw-mi give), de/deig-mai (dei/k-nu_-mi show). On the euphonic changes of consonants, see 409.

§574 D
A thematic vowel precedes the ending in Hom. me/mbletai (me/lw care for), o)rw/retai (o')rnumi rouse).

§575
The stem of the perfect middle is in general the same as that of the first perfect active as regards its vowel (557), the retention or expulsion of n (559 a), and metathesis (559 d).
ti_ma/-w honour teti/_mh-mai e)teti_mh/mhn; poie/-w make pepoi/h-mai e)pepoih/mhn; gra/f-w write ge/gram-mai; kri/_nw (krin-) judge ke/kri-mai; tei/nw (ten-) stretch te/tamai; fqei/rw (fqer-) corrupt e)/fqar-mai; ba/llw (bal-) throw be/blh-mai e)beblh/mhn; pei/qw (piq-, peiq-, poiq-) persuade pe/peismai e)pepei/smhn.

§576
The vowel of the perfect middle stem should show the weak form when there is variation between e (ei, eu): o (oi, ou): a (i, u). The weak form in a appears regularly in verbs containing a liquid (479): that in u, in pe/pusmai from punqa/nomai (puq-, peuq-) learn, poet. e)/ssumai hasten from seu/w (su-, seu-) urge.

§577
The vowel of the present has often displaced the weak form, as in pe/plegmai (ple/k-w weave), le/leimmai (lei/p-w leave), pe/peismai (pei/q-w persuade), e)/zeugmai (zeu/g-nu_-mi yoke).

§578
A final short vowel of the verb-stem is not lengthened in the verbs given in 488 a. e is added (485) in many verbs. For metathesis see 492; for Attic reduplication see 446.

§579

n is retained in endings not beginning with m, as fai/nw (fan-) show, pe/fantai, pe/fanqe. Before -mai, we have m in w)/cummai from o)cu/_nw (o)cun-) sharpen, but usually n is replaced by s. On the insertion of s, see 489.

§580

Future Perfect.—The stem of the future perfect is formed by adding -so/e- to the stem of the perfect middle. A vowel immediately preceding -so/e- is always long, though it may have been short in the perfect middle.
lu/_-w loose, lelu/_-somai I shall have been loosed (perf. mid. le/lu^-mai), de/-w bind dedh/-somai (perf. mid. de/de-mai), gra/f-w write gegra/y-omai, kale/w call keklh/somai.

§580 D
Hom. has dede/couai, memnh/somai, keklh/sh|, kexolw/setai; kekadh/somai, pefidh/setai are from reduplicated aorists.

§581
The future perfect usually has a passive force. The active meaning is found where the perfect middle or active has an active meaning (1946, 1947).
kekth/somai shall possess (ke/kthmai possess), kekra/_comai shall cry out (ke/kra_ga cry out), kekla/gcomai shall scream (ke/klagga scream), memnh/somai shall remember (me/mnhmai remember), pepau/somai shall have ceased (pe/paumai have ceased).

§582
Not all verbs can form a future perfect; and few forms of this tense occur outside of the indicative: diapepolemhso/menon Thuc. 7. 25 is the only sure example of the participle in classical Greek. The infinitive memnh/sesqai occurs in Hom. and Attic prose.

§583
The periphrastic construction (601) of the perfect middle (passive) participle with e)/somai may be used for the future perfect, as e)yeusme/nos e)/somai I shall have been deceived.

§584

Future Perfect Active.—The future perfect active of most verbs is formed periphrastically (600). Two perfects with a present meaning, e(/sthka I stand (i(/sthmi set) and te/qnhka I am dead (qnh/|skw), form the future perfects e(sth/cw I shall stand, teqnh/cw I shall be dead.

§584 D
Hom. has kexarh/sw and kexarh/somai from xai/rw (xar-) rejoice.

## VIII. FIRST PASSIVE SYSTEM (*q*h PASSIVE)

## (FIRST AORIST AND FIRST FUTURE PASSIVE)

## FIRST AORIST PASSIVE

§585
The stem of the first aorist passive is formed by adding -qh- (or -qe-) directly to the verb-stem: e)-lu/-qh-n I was loosed, e)-fa/n-qh-n I was shown (fai/nw, fan-), e)-do/-qh-n I was given (di/dwmi, do-, dw-).
a. -qh- appears in the indicative, imperative (except the third plural), and infinitive; -qe- appears in the other moods. -qh- is found before a single consonant, -qe- before two consonants or a vowel except in the nom. neuter of the participle.

§585 a. D
For -qhsan we find -qen in Hom., as die/kriqen.

§586
The verb-stem agrees with that of the perfect middle herein:
a. Vowel verbs lengthen the final vowel of the verb-stem, as te-ti/_mh-mai, e)-ti_mh/-qhn. On verbs which do not lengthen their final vowel, see 488.
b. Liquid stems of one syllable change e to a, as te/-ta-mai, e)-ta/-qhn (tei/nw stretch, ten-). But stre/fw turn, tre/pw turn, tre/fw nourish have e)stre/fqhn, e)tre/fqhn, e)qre/fqhn (rare), though the perfect middles are e)/strammai, te/trammai, te/qrammai.

§586 b. D

e)stra/fqhn is Ionic and Doric; Hom. and Hdt. have e)tra/fqhn from tre/pw. Hom. has e)ta/rfqhn and e)te/rfqhn from te/rpw gladden.
c. Primitive verbs showing in their stems the gradations e (ei, eu): o (oi, ou): a (i, u) have a strong form, as e)tre/fqhn from tre/pw (trep-, trop-, trap-) turn, e)lei/fqhn from lei/pw (lip-, leip-, loip-) leave, e)pleu/sqhn from ple/w (plu-, pleu-) sail.
d. Primitive verbs showing in their stems a variation between e: h and o: w have, in the first aorist passive, the short vowel. Thus, ti/qhmi (qe-, qh-) e)te/qhn, di/dwmi (do-, dw-) e)do/qhn.
e. Final n is dropped in some verbs: ke/-kri-mai, e)kri/qhn. See 491.

§586 e. D
Hom. has e)kli/nqhn and e)kli/qhn, e)kri/nqhn and e)kri/qhn; i(dru/nqhn = Att. i(dru/_qhn (i(dru/w erect), a)mpnu/nqhn (a)napne/w revive).
f. The verb-stem may suffer metathesis: be/-blh-mai, e)-blh/-qhn. See 492.
g. Sigma is often added: ke-ke/leus-mai, e)-keleu/s-qhn. See 489.

§587
Before q of the suffix, p and b become f; k and g become x (82 c); t, d, q become s (83). f and x remain unaltered.
lei/p-w e)lei/f-qhn, bla/ptw (blab-) e)bla/f-qhn; fula/ttw (fulak-) e)fula/x-qhn, a)/g-w h)/x-qhn; komi/zw (komid-) e)komi/s-qhn, pei/q-w e)pei/s-qhn; gra/f-w e)gra/f-qhn, tara/ttw (tarax-) e)tara/x-qhn.

§588

q of the verb-stem becomes t in e)-te/-qhn, and in e)-tu/-qhn for e)-qu-qhn from ti/qhmi (qe-, qh-) place and qu/_w (qu-, qu_-) sacrifice. See 125 c.

## FIRST FUTURE PASSIVE

§589
The stem of the first future passive is formed by adding -so/e- to the stem of the first aorist passive. It ends in -qhsomai. Thus, paideuqh/-somai I shall be educated, luqh/-somai I shall be loosed.
ti_ma/w, e)ti_mh/qhn ti_mhqh/somai; e)a/w, ei)a/_qhn e)a_qh/somai; lei/pw, e)lei/fqhn leifqh/somai; pei/qw, e)pei/sqhn peisqh/somai; tei/nw, e)ta/qhn taqh/somai; ta/ttw, e)ta/xqhn taxqh/somai; ti/qhmi, e)te/qhn teqh/somai; di/dwmi, e)do/qhn doqh/somai; dei/knu_mi, e)dei/xqhn deixqh/somai.

§589 D
Hom. has no example of the first future passive. To express the idea of the passive future the future middle is used. See 802. Doric shows the active endings in both futures passive: deixqhsou=nti, a)nagrafhsei=.

## IX. SECOND PASSIVE SYSTEM (H PASSIVE)

## (SECOND AORIST AND SECOND FUTURE PASSIVE)

## SECOND AORIST PASSIVE

§590
The stem of the second aorist passive is formed by adding -h- (or -e-) directly to the verb-stem. Thus, e)bla/bhn I was injured from bla/ptw (blab-).
a. -h- appears in the indicative, imperative (except the third plural), and infinitive; -e- appears in the other moods. -h- is found before a single consonant, -e- before two consonants or a vowel except in the nom. neut. of the participle.

§590 a. D
For -hsan we generally find -en (from -hnt, 40) in Hom.; also in Doric.

§591
The second aorist passive agrees in form with the second aorist active of mi-verbs; cp. intransitive e)xa/rhn rejoiced with e)/sthn stood. The passive use was developed from the intransitive use.

§592
Primitive verbs showing in their stems the grades e: o: a have a. Thus an e of a monosyllabic verb-stem becomes a, as in ple/k-w weave e)pla/khn, kle/p-t-w steal e)kla/phn, fqei/rw (fqer-) corrupt e)fqa/rhn, ste/llw (stel-) send e)sta/lhn. But le/gw collect has e)le/ghn.

§593
Primitive verbs showing in their stems a variation between a short and long vowel have, in the second aorist passive, the short vowel. Thus th/kw (tak-, thk-) melt e)ta/khn, r(h/gnu_mi (r(ag-, r(hg-, r(wg-) break e)rra/ghn.
a. But plh/ttw (plag-, plhg-) strike has e)pla/ghn only in composition, as e)cepla/ghn; otherwise e)plh/ghn.

§594
The second aorist passive is the only aorist passive formed in Attic prose by a)/gnu_mi (e)a/_ghn), gra/fw (e)gra/fhn), de/rw (e)da/rhn), qa/ptw (e)ta/fhn), ko/ptw (e)ko/phn), mai/nw (e)ma/nhn), pni/_gw (e)pni^/ghn), r(a/ptw (e)rra/fhn), r(e/w (e)rru/hn active), r(h/gnu_mi (e)rra/ghn), sh/pw (e)sa/phn), ska/ptw (e)ska/fhn), spei/rw (e)spa/rhn), ste/llw (e)sta/lhn), sfa/zw or sfa/ttw (e)sfa/ghn), sfa/llw (e)sfa/lhn), tu/_fw (e)tu/fhn), fqei/rw (e)fqa/rhn pass. and intr.), fu/_w (in subj. fuw=), xai/rw (e)xa/rhn active).

§595
Both the first aorist passive and the second aorist passive are formed by a)lei/fw (h)lei/fqhn), a)lla/ttw (-hlla/xqhn, h)lla/ghn), ba/ptw (e)ba/fhn), bla/ptw (e)bla/fqhn, e)bla/bhn), bre/xw (e)bre/xqhn), zeu/gnu_mi (e)zu/ghn), qli/_bw (e)qli/_fqhn), kle/ptw (e)kla/phn), kli/_nw (-ekli/nhn), kru/ptw (e)kru/fqhn), le/gw collect (diele/xqhn, but sunele/ghn), ma/ttw (e)ma/ghn), mei/gnu_mi (e)mi/ghn), ph/gnu_mi (e)pa/ghn), ple/kw (e)pla/khn), plh/ttw (e)plh/ghn and -epla/ghn), r(i/_ptw (e)rri/_fqhn, e)rri/fhn), steri/skw (e)sterh/qhn), stre/fw (e)stra/fhn), ta/ttw (e)ta/xqhn), th/kw (e)ta/khn), tre/pw (e)tra/phn pass. and intr.), tre/fw (e)tra/fhn pass. and intr.), tri/_bw (e)tri/bhn, e)tri/_fqhn), fai/nw (e)fa/nqhn was shown, e)fa/nhn appeared), fra/gnu_mi (e)fra/xqhn), yu/_xw (e)yu/xhn). Most of these verbs use either the one in prose and the other in poetry, the dialects, or late Greek. Only the forms in common prose use are inserted in brackets.

§596
Only those verbs which have no second aorist active show the second aorist passive; except tre/pw, which has all the aorists: active e)/treya and e)/trapon turned; middle e)treya/mhn put to flight, e)trapo/mhn turned myself, took to flight; passive e)tre/fqhn was turned, e)tra/phn was turned and turned myself.

## SECOND FUTURE PASSIVE

§597
The stem of the second future passive is formed by adding -s o/e- to the stem of the second aorist passive. It ends in -hsomai. Thus, blhbh/somai I shall be injured from bla/ptw (blab-) e)-bla/bh-n.
ko/p-t-w, e)ko/phn koph/somai; gra/fw, e)gra/fhn grafh/somai; fai/nw, e)fa/nhn appeared, fanh/somai; fqei/rw, e)fqa/rhn fqarh/somai; ph/gnu_mi fix, e)pa/ghn pagh/somai.

§597 D
Hom. has only dah/seai (e)da/hn learned), migh/sesqai (mei/gnu_mi mix).

§598
Most of the verbs in 594, 595 form second futures passive except a)/gnu_mi, a)lei/fw, ba/ptw, bre/xw, zeu/gnu_mi, qli/_bw, kle/ptw, mai/nw, ma/ttw, r(a/ptw. But many of the second futures appear only in poetry or in late Greek, and some are found only in composition.

## PERIPHRASTIC FORMS

§599

Perfect.—For the simple perfect and pluperfect periphrastic forms are often used.
a. For the perfect or pluperfect active indicative the forms of the perfect active participle and ei)mi/ or h)=n may be used: as lelukw/s ei)mi for le/luka, lelukw\s h)=n for e)lelu/kh. So bebohqhko/tes h)=san for e)bebohqh/kesan (bohqe/w come to aid); ei)mi\ teqhkw\s for te/qhka I have placed; gegrafw\s h)=n for e)gegra/fh I had written; peponqw\s h)=n I had suffered. Such forms are more common in the pluperfect and in general denote state rather than action.
b. For the perfect active a periphrasis of the aorist participle and e)/xw is sometimes used, especially when a perfect active form with transitive meaning is lacking; as sth/sa_s e)/xw I have placed (e(/sthka, intransitive, stand), e)rasqei\s e)/xw I have loved. So often because the aspirated perfect is not used, as e)/xeis tara/ca_s thou hast stirred up. Cp. habeo with the perfect participle.
c. In the perfect active subjunctive and optative the forms in -kw and -koimi are very rare. In their place the perfect active participle with w)= and ei)/hn is usually employed: lelukw\s (leloipw\s) w)=, ei)/hn. Other forms than 3 sing. and 3 pl. are rare. Cp. 691, 694.
d. The perfect or pluperfect passive is often paraphrased by the perfect participle and e)sti/ or h)=n; as gegramme/non e)sti/ it stands written, e)sti\ dedogme/non it stands resolved, parhggelme/non h)=n = parh/ggelto (paragge/llw give orders).
e. In the third plural of the perfect and pluperfect middle (passive) the perfect middle participle with ei)si/ (h)=san) is used when a stem ending in a consonant would come in direct contact with the endings -ntai, -nto. See 408.
f. The perfect subjunctive and optative middle are formed by the perfect middle participle with w)= or ei)/hn: lelume/nos w)=, ei)/hn.
g. The perfect imperative of all voices may be expressed by combining the perfect participle with i)/sqi, e)/stw (697). lelukw\s i)/sqi loose, etc., ei)rhme/non e)/stw let it have been said, gegonw\s e)/stw
P. L. 951c, gegono/tes e)/stwsan
P. L. 779d.
h. Periphrasis of the infinitive is rare:

teqnhko/ta ei)=nai to be dead
X. C. 1.4.11.

§600

Future Perfect Active.—The future perfect active of most verbs is formed by combining the perfect active participle with e)/somai shall be. Thus, gegrafw\s e)/somai I shall have written, cp. scriptus ero. For the two verbs which do not use this periphrasis, see 584.
a. The perfect middle participle is used in the case of deponent verbs: a)poleloghme/nos e)/somai
And. 1.72.

§601

Future Perfect Passive.—The future perfect passive may be expressed by using the perfect middle (passive) participle with e)/somai shall be. Thus, e)yeusme/noi e)/sesqe you will have been deceived.

## FIRST CONJUGATION OR VERBS IN *w

§602
Verbs in -w have the thematic vowel -o/e (-w/h-) between the tense-stem and the personal endings in the present system. The name “w-conjugation,” or “thematic conjugation,” is applied to all verbs which form the present and imperfect with the thematic vowel.

§603
Inflected according to the w-conjugation are all thematic presents and imperfects; those second aorists active and middle in which the tense-stem ends with the thematic vowel; all futures, all first aorists active and middle; and most perfects and pluperfects active.

§604
Certain tenses of verbs ending in -w in the first person present indicative active, or of deponent verbs in which the personal endings are preceded by the thematic vowel, are inflected without the thematic vowel, herein agreeing with mi-verbs. These tenses are: all aorists passive; all perfects and pluperfects middle and passive; a few second perfects and pluperfects active; and those second aorists active and middle in which the tense-stem does not end with the thematic vowel. But all subjunctives are thematic.

§605
Verbs in -w fall into two main classes, distinguished by the last letter of the verb-stem:
1. Vowel verbs: a. Uncontracted verbs. b. Contracted verbs.
2. Consonant verbs: a. Liquid verbs. b. Stop (or mute) verbs.
N. Under 2 fall also (c) those verbs whose stems ended in s or v (624).

§606

Vowel Verbs.—Vowel verbs usually do not form second aorists, second perfects, and second futures in the passive. A vowel short in the present is commonly lengthened in the other tenses. Vowel verbs belong to the first class of present stems (498-504; but see 612).

§607

Vowel Verbs not contracted.—Vowel verbs not contracted have verb-stems ending in i_^, u_^, or in a diphthong (ai, ei, au, eu, ou).
（i) e)sqi/w eat, pri/_w saw, xri/_w anoint, poet. di/w fear, ti/_w honour (500. 2); (u) a)nu/w accomplish, mequ/w am intoxicated, lu/_w loose, qu/_w sacrifice, fu/_w produce, kwlu/_w hinder (and many others, 500. 1 a); (ai) knai/w scratch, pai/w strike, ptai/w stumble, palai/w wrestle, a)gai/omai am indignant, dai/w kindle, dai/omai divide, lilai/omai desire eagerly, poet. mai/omai desire, nai/w dwell, r(ai/w strike; (ei) klh/w (later klei/w) shut, sei/w shake, Epic kei/w split and rest; (au) au(/w kindle, qrau/w break, a)polau/w enjoy, pau/w make cease (pau/omai cease), poet. i)au/w rest; (eu) basileu/w am king, bouleu/w consult (bouleu/omai deliberate), qhreu/w hunt, keleu/w order, leu/w stone, paideu/w educate, xoreu/w dance, foneu/w slay. Most verbs in -euw are either denominatives, as basileu/w from basileu/s; or are due to the analogy of such denominatives, as paideu/w. geu/omai taste is a primitive. qe/w run, ne/w swim, ple/w sail, pne/w breathe, r(e/w flow, xe/w pour have forms in eu, u; cp. poet. seu/w urge, a)leu/w avert, a)xeu/w am grieved; (ou) a)kou/w hear, kolou/w dock, krou/w beat, lou/w wash.

§608
Some primitive vowel verbs in -iw, -uw (522) formed their present stem by the aid of the suffix [iglide] (y), which has been lost. Denominatives in -iw, -uw, -euw regularly added the suffix, as poet. mhni/-w am wroth from mhni-[iglide]w (mh=ni-s wrath), poet. dakru/_w weep (da/kru tear), poet. fi_tu/_-w beget from fi_tu-[iglide]w, mequ/w am drunk, basileu/w am king. Poet. dhri/_omai, masti/w, mhti/omai, khki/w, a)xlu/w, ghru/w, i)qu/w.

§609
The stem of some of the uncontracted vowel verbs originally ended in s or v (624).

§610
Some verbs with verb-stems in vowels form presents in -nw (523), as pi/_nw drink, fqi/_nw perish; and in -skw (526).

§611

Vowel Verbs contracted.—Vowel verbs that contract have verb-stems ending in a, e, o, with some in a_, h, w.

§612
All contracted verbs form their present stem by the help of the suffix [iglide] (y), and properly belong to the Third Class (522).

§613
Some contracted verbs have verb-stems which originally ended in s or v (624).

§614

Liquid Verbs.—Liquid verbs have verb-stems in l, m, n, r.
The present is rarely formed from the simple verb-stem, as in me/n-w remain; ordinarily the suffix [iglide] (y) is added, as in ste/llw (stel-[iglide]w) send, kri/_nw (kri^n-[iglide]w) judge, ktei/nw (kten-[iglide]w) slay, fai/nw (fan-[iglide]w) show.

§614 D

pefu/rsesqai in Pindar is made from fu/rsw (fu/_rw knead).

§615
A short vowel of the verb-stem remains short in the future but is lengthened in the first aorist (544). Thus:
a. a in the future, h in the aorist: fai/nw (fan-) show, fanw=, e)/fhna. In this class fall all verbs in -ainw, -airw, -allw.
b. e in the future, ei in the aorist: me/n-w remain, menw=, e)/meina; ste/llw (stel-) send, stelw=, e)/steila. Here belong verbs in -ellw, -emw, -emnw, -erw, -eirw, -enw, -einw.
c. i^ in the future, i_ in the aorist: kli/_nw (klin-) incline, kli^nw=, e)/kli_na. Here belong verbs in -illw, -i_nw, -i_rw.
d. u^ in the future, u_ in the aorist: su/_rw (sur-) drag, su^rw=, e)/su_ra. Here belong verbs in -u_rw, -u_nw.
For the formation of the future stem see 535, of the aorist stem see 544.

§616
For the perfect stem see 559. Few liquid verbs make second perfects. On the change of e, a of the verb-stem to o, h in the second perfect, see 478, 484.
Liquid verbs with futures in -w= do not form future perfects.

§617
Monosyllabic verb-stems containing e have a in the first perfect active, perfect middle, first aorist and future passive and in all second aorists, but o in the second perfect. Thus, fqei/rw (fqer-) corrupt, e)/fqarka, e)/fqarmai, e)fqa/rhn, but di-e/fqora have destroyed (819).

§618
A few monosyllabic stems do not change e to a in the 2 aor., as te/mnw cut e)/temon (but e)/tamon in Hom., Hdt. etc.), gi/gnomai (gen-) become e)geno/mhn. See also qei/nw, qe/romai, ke/lomai, root fen-. Few liquid verbs form second aorists.

§619
Stems of more than one syllable do not change the vowel of the verb-stem.

§621

Stop Verbs.—Many verb stems end in a stop (or mute) consonant.
The present is formed either from the simple verb-stem, as in ple/k-w weave, or by the addition of t or [iglide] (y) to the verb-stem, as in bla/ptw (blab-) injure, fula/ttw (fulak-[iglide]w) guard. All tenses except the present and imperfect are formed without the addition of t or i= to the verb-stem; thus, bla/yw from blab-s-w, fula/cw from fulak-s-w.

§622
Some monosyllabic stems show a variation in the quantity of the stem vowel i or u, as tri/_bw rub perf. te/tri^fa, yu/_xw cool 2 aor. pass. e)yu^/xhn, th/kw melt (Doric ta/_kw) 2 aor. pass. e)ta^/khn. Cp. 475, 477 c, 500. Many monosyllabic stems show qualitative vowel gradation: i ei oi; u eu ou; a h w; a e o. For examples see 477-484.

## INFLECTION OF *w-VERBS

§625
Verbs which end in w in the first person present indicative active, and deponent verbs in which the personal endings are preceded by the thematic vowel, have the following peculiarities of inflection:
a. The thematic vowel usually appears in all tenses except the perfect and pluperfect middle (passive) and the aorist passive (except in the subjunctive). These three tenses are inflected like mi-verbs.
b. The present and future singular active end in -w, -eis, -ei (463). The ending -mi appears only in the optative.
c. The thematic vowel o unites in the indicative with the ending -nti, and forms -ousi (463 d).
d. The third plural active of past tenses ends in -n.
e. The imperative active has no personal ending in the second person singular except -o-n in the first aorist.
f. Except in the perfect and pluperfect the middle endings -sai and -so lose s and contract with the final vowel of the tense-stem (465 a, b). In the optative contraction cannot take place (lu/_oi-（s）o, lu/_sai-（s）o).
g. The infinitive active has -ein (for -e-en) in the present, future, and second aorist; -e-nai in the perfect; and -ai in the aorist.
h. Active participles with stems in -ont- have the nominative masculine in -wn.

§626
In 627-716 the method of inflection of all w-verbs, both vowel and consonant, is described. The examples are generally taken from vowel verbs, but the statements hold true of consonant verbs.
Forms of w-verbs which are inflected according to the non-thematic conjugation are included under the w-verbs.

## PRESENT AND IMPERFECT ACTIVE AND MIDDLE (PASSIVE)

For the formation of the present stem see 497-531.

§627

Indicative.—Vowel and consonant verbs in -w inflect the present by attaching the primary endings (when there are any) to the present stem in -o/e (-w/h-). lu/_w, ti_mw= (ti_ma/-w), fai/nw, lei/pw. The imperfect attaches the secondary endings to the present stem with the augment. See the paradigms, pp. 114, 120. For the active forms -w, -eis, -ei, see 463.

§628

-h| and -ei are found in the pres. fut. mid. and pass., fut. perf. pass. e-（s）ai yields h| (written EI in the Old Attic alphabet, 2 a), which is usually given as the proper spelling in the texts of the tragic poets, whereas ei is printed in the texts of prose and comedy. ei was often written for hi (h|) after 400 B.C., as in a)gaqei= tu/xei, since both had the sound of a close long e. It is often impossible to settle the spelling; but bou/lei wishest, oi)/ei thinkest, and o)/yei shalt see (from o(ra/w) have only the -ei forms. -ei is sometimes called Attic and Ionic in contrast to -h| of the other dialects, including the Koiné.

§629

Subjunctive.—The present subjunctive adds the primary endings to the tense-stem with the long thematic vowel. For the endings -h|s, -h| see 463. Thus, lu/_w, -h|s, -h|, ti_ma=|s ( = ti_ma/-h|s), ti_ma=| ( = ti_ma/-h|), fai/nwmen, -hte, -wsi (from -wnti). Middle lu/_w-mai, lu/_h| ( = lu/_h-sai), lu/_h-tai; ti_ma=-sqon ( = ti_ma/h-sqon); fainw/-meqa, fai/nh-sqe, fai/nw-ntai.

§630

Optative.—To the tense-stem ending in the thematic vowel (always o) are added the mood-sign -i_- (-ie-) or -ih- (459, 460) and the secondary personal endings (except -mi for -n, where the mood sign is -i_-, 459). In the 3 pl. we have -ie-n.
a. The final vowel of the tense-stem (o) contracts with the mood suffix (i_), o-i_ becoming oi. Thus lu/_oimi (lu/_o-i_-mi), lu/_ois (lu/_o-i_-s), lu/_oien (lu/_o-ie-n), lu_oi/mhn (lu_o-i/_-mhn), lu/_oio (lu/_o-i_-so).

§631

Imperative.—The present imperative endings are added to the tensestem with the thematic vowel e (o before -ntwn). The 2 pers. sing. active has no ending, but uses the tense-stem instead (pai/deue, fai=ne). In the middle -so loses its s (466, 2 a); lu/_ou from lu/_e-so, fai/nou from fai/ne-so. On the forms in -etwsan and -esqwsan for -ontwn and -esqwn, see 466, 2 b.

§632

Infinitive.—The present stem unites with -en: lu/_e-en = lu/_ein, lei/pe-en = lei/pein. In the middle (passive) -sqai is added: lu/_e-sqai, lei/pe-sqai.

§632 D
Severer Doric has e)/xhn and e)/xen; Milder Doric has e)/xein; Aeolic has e)/xhn. Hom. has a)mu/_nein, a)mu_ne/menai, a)mu_ne/men.

§633

Participle.—The present participle adds -nt- to the present stem ending in the thematic vowel o. Stems in -o-nt have the nominative singular in -wn. Thus masc. lu/_wn from lu_ont-s, fem. lu/_ousa from lu_ont-[iglide]a, neut. lu=on from lu_on（t). See 301 a and N.

§633 D
Aeolic has fem. -oisa in the present and second aorist (37 D. 3), lu/_oisa, li/poisa.

§634
A few w-verbs in the present and imperfect show forms of the mi-conjugation. These are usually Epic.
de/xomai, 3 pl. de/xatai await for dexṇtai, part. de/gmenos, imperf. e)de/gmhn. But these are often regarded as perfect and pluperfect without reduplication. e)de/gmhn in some passages is a second aorist (688).—e)/dw eat (529. 5), inf. e)/dmenai.—e)ru/w (or ei)ru/w) in ei)ru/atai.—lou=tai wash is from lo/etai, not from lou/w (cp. 398 a).— oi)=mai think is probably a perfect to oi)/omai (oi)-o-).—ou)ta/w wound in ou)=ta, ou)ta/menai is 2 aor.—fe/rw bear, imper. fe/rte.

## CONTRACT VERBS

§635
Verbs in -aw, -ew, -ow contract the final a, e, o of the verb-stem with the thematic vowel -o/e (-w/h) in the present and imperfect tenses. Thus, ti_ma/w ti_mw=, poie/w poiw=, dhlo/w dhlw=; e)ti/_maon e)ti/_mwn, e)poi/eon e)poi/oun, e)dh/loon e)dh/loun. The rules of contraction are given in 4955; the paradigms, p. 120.
a. Open forms of -ew verbs occur in the lyric parts of tragedy.

§636

Subjunctive.—The subjunctive adds the primary endings. For the contractions see 59.

§637

Optative.—a/oi becomes w=|, e/oi and o/oi become oi=. Thus. -a/o-i_-mi = -w=|mi, -ao-i/h-n = -w/|hn, -ao-i/_-mhn = -w/|mhn; -e/o-i_-mi = -oi=mi, -eo-i/h-n = -oi/hn, -eo-i/_-mhn = -oi/mhn; -o/o-i_-mi = -oi=mi, -o-i/h-n = -oi/hn, -oo-i/_-mhn = -oi/mhn. Thus, ti_mw/|hn (ti_mao-i/h-n), ti_mw/|hs (ti_mao-i/h-s), ti_mw/|h (ti_mao-i/h), ti_mw/|mhn (ti_mao-i/_-mhn), poioi=o (poie/o-i_-so), poioi=to (poie/o-i_-to).

§638
In the singular -aw verbs usually end in -w/|hn, -w/|hs, -w/h|, rarely in -w=|mi, -w=|s, -w=|. -ew verbs usually end in -oi/hn, -oi/hs, -oi/h, rarely in -oi=mi, -oi=s, -oi= (-oi= chiefly in Plato).

§639
In the dual and plural -aw verbs usually end in -w=|ton, -w/|thn, -w=|men, -w=|te, -w=|en, rarely in -w/|hton, -w|h/thn, -w/|hmen, -w/|hte, -w/|hsan. -ew verbs usually end in -oi=ton, -oi/thn, -oi=men, -oi=te, -oi=en, rarely in -oi/hton, -oih/thn, -oi/hmen, -oi/hte, -oi/hsan.

§640
Few cases of the optative of -ow verbs occur. In the sing. both -oi/hn and -oi=mi are found; in the plur. -oi=men, -oi=te, -oi=en. For r(i_gw/|hn from r(i_go/w shiver see 641.

§641
Several contract verbs have stems in -a_, -h, -w.
These are the verbs of 394, 398 with apparently irregular contraction, and drw= do; with presents made from -a_-[iglide]w, -h-[iglide]w, -w-[iglide]w. Thus, from zh/w, zh/eis, zh/ei and xrh/omai, xrh/e（s）ai, xrh/etai come zw=, zh=|s, zh=| and xrw=mai, xrh=|, xrh=tai; so diyh=n, peinh=n from diyh/-en, peinh/-en. i/dro/w, r(i_go/w (398) derive the forms in w and w| from i(drw-, r(i_gw- (i(drw/w, r(i_gw/w from i(drws-[iglide]w, r(i_gws-[iglide]w). The forms in -ow are from the weaker stems i)dros-, r(i_gos-.

§641 D
Hom. has diya/_wn, peina/_wn, peinh/menai, mna/_omai, xrh/wn (Mss. xrei/wn) uttering oracles, gelw/w, i(drw/w. The verbs in 394, except diyw= and peinw=, have stems in h and a^ (36 e); thus, in Hdt., xra=tai from xra/etai, but xre/w imper., xrew/menos from xrh=o, xrho/menos by 34. Hom. and Ion. zw/w has the stem zw (zw-[iglide]w). Hdt. has zh=n, diyh=n, but kna=n, sma=n.

## CONTRACT VERBS IN THE DIALECTS

§642

-aw Verbs in Homer.—Hom. leaves -aw verbs open 64 times, as naieta/w, -a/ousi, u(la/ei, a)oidia/ousa, goa/oimen, thleqa/ontas. When contracted, -aw verbs have the Attic forms, as o(rw=, o(ra=|s, o(ra=|; as peira=| makest trial from peira/e-（s）ai from peira/omai; h)rw= didst pray from h)ra/e-（s）o from a)ra/omai.

§643
When uncontracted, verbs in -aw often show in the Mss. of Hom., not the original open forms, but “assimilated” forms of the concurrent vowels, ae, aei, ah giving a double a sound by a prevailing over the e sound; ao, aw, aoi, aou giving a double o sound by the o sound prevailing over the a. One of the vowels is commonly lengthened, rarely both.

ae = (1)aa: o(ra/esqai = o(ra/asqai, a)ga/-

esqe = a)ga/asqe.

= (2)a_a: mna/esqai = mna/_asqai, h)ga/-

esqe = h)ga/_asqe.

N.—a)lo/w from a)la/eo wander is unique. gelw/ontes is from gelw/w (641).

§644
The assimilated forms are used only when the second vowel (in the unchanged form) stood in a syllable long by nature or position. Hence o(rowmen, o(raate, o(raato, do not occur for o(ra/omen, etc. (mnwo/menos for mna_o/menos is an exception.) The first vowel is lengthened only when the metre requires it, as in h(bw/ontes for h(ba/ontes ¯ ˘ ¯ ˘. Thus two long vowels do not occur in succession except to fit the form to the verse, as menoinw/w for menoina/w; but h(bw/oimi, not h(bw/w|mi. When the first vowel is metrically lengthened, the second vowel is not lengthened, though it may be long either in a final syllable (as in menoina/_a|) or when it represents the spurious diphthong ou from -ont- (as in h(bw/wsa, drw/wsi for h(ba/ousa, dra/_ousi from -ont[iglide]a, -onti).

§645
The assimilated forms include the “Attic” future in -aw from -asw (539); as e)lo/wsi ( = e)la/ousi), kremo/w, dama/a|, damo/wsi.

§646
The assimilated forms are found only in the artificial language of Homer, Hesiod, and their imitators, and nowhere in the living speech. They are commonly explained as derived from the contracted forms by a process of ‘distraction,’ and as inserted in the text for the sake of the metre. Thus o(ra=|s, bow=ntes, the spoken forms which had taken the place of original o(ra/eis, boa/ontes, in the text, were expanded into o(ra/a|s, boo/wntes, by repetition of the a and o. While the restoration of the original uncontracted forms is generally possible, and is adopted in several modern editions, a phonetic origin of many of the forms in question is still sought by some scholars who regard o(ro/w as an intermediate stage between o(ra/w and o(rw=. It will be observed, however, that the forms in 648 can be derived only from the unassimilated forms.

§647
In the imperfect contraction generally occurs, and assimilation is rare.

§648
Some verbs show eo for ao, as h)/nteon, tro/peon, menoi/neon, pote/ontai. Cp. 649, 653.

§649

-aw verbs in Herodotus.—Hdt. contracts -aw verbs as they are contracted in Attic. In many cases before an o sound the Mss. substitute e for a (tolme/w, o(re/wn, e)foi/teon). This e is never found in all the forms of the same verb, and the Mss. generally disagree on each occurrence of any form.—Hdt. always has -w/|hn, -w/|mhn, in the optative.

§650

-ew verbs in Homer.—a. Hom. rarely contracts ew and eo (except in the participle). In a few cases eu appears for eo, as poieu/mhn; rarely for eou, as teleu=si. When the metre allows either -ee and -eei, or -ei, the open forms are slightly more common. ei is often necessary to admit a word into the verse (as h(gei=sqai, e)fi/lei), and is often found at the verse-end. -e/-e-ai, -e/-e-o, in the 2 sing. mid. may become -ei=ai, -ei=o, or -e/ai, -e/o, by the expulsion of one e; as mu_qei=ai or mu_qe/ai sayest, ai)dei=o show regard.
b. neikei/w, telei/w, from -es-[iglide]w (neikes-, teles-) are older forms than neike/w, tele/w. See 488 d, 624. qei/w, plei/w, pnei/w show metrical lengthening (28 D.).
c. On -hmenai in Hom. see 657.

§651

-ew verbs in Herodotus.—a. Hdt. generally leaves eo, ew, eou, open, except when a vowel precedes the e, in which case we find eu for eo (a)gnoeu=ntes). In the 3 plur. -e/ousi is kept except in poieu=si. For -e/-eo in the 2 sing. mid. we find e/-o in ai)te/o. ee, eei, in stems of more than one syllable, are usually uncontracted in the Mss., but this is probably an error. dei= it is necessary and dei=n are never written otherwise.—The Ion. eu for eo, eou, occurs rarely in tragedy.
b. In the optative Hdt. has -e/oi after a consonant, as kale/oi, but -oi= after a vowel, as poioi=mi, poioi=.

§652

Verbs in -ow.—a. Hom. always uses the contracted forms except in the case of such as show assimilation like that in -aw verbs.

oo = (1) ow : dhi+o/onto = dhi+o/wnto.ooi = ow| : dhio/oien = dhio/w|en.

(2) wo : u(pno/ontas = u(pnw/ontas.oou = ow : a)ro/ousi = a)ro/wsi.
b. Hdt. contracts -ow verbs as in Attic. Forms with eu for ou, as dikaieu=si, e)dikai/eun, are incorrect.

§653

Doric.—Doric (59 D.) contracts ae and ah to h; aei and ah| to h|; ao, aw, to a_ except in final syllables: ti_mw=, ti_mh=|s, ti_mh=|, ti_ma=mes, ti_mh=te, ti_ma=nti, ti/_mh, ti_mh=n. Monosyllabic stems have w from a + o or a + w. Some verbs in -aw have alternative forms in -ew (648), as o(re/w, ti_me/w.

§654
The contractions of -ew verbs in Doric may be illustrated thus:
