e)f' oi(=s th\n ei)rh/nhn e)poihsa/meqa on what terms we made the peace
D. 8.5. Reason, motive, end, as with verbs of emotion (instead of the simple dative, 1517): pa/nta tau=ta qauma/zw e)pi\ tw=| ka/llei I am astonished at all these trees because of their beauty
X. O. 4.21, ou)k e)pi\ te/xnh| e)/maqes a)ll' e)pi\ paidei/a| you learned this not to make it a profession but to gain general culture
P. Pr. 312b. Hostility (less common in prose than in poetry; usually with accus.):

h( e)pi\ tw=| *mh/dw| cummaxi/a_ the alliance against the Medes
T. 3.63. Price: e)pi\ po/sw|; for how much?
P. A. 41a.

## 3. e)pi/ with the Accusative

a. Local: of the goal:

e)celau/nei e)pi\ to\n potamo/n he marches to the river
X. A. 1.4.11, a)fi/_konto e)pi\ to\n potamo/n they arrived at the river 4. 7. 18 (rarely the gen. with verbs of arrival),

a)ne/bainen e)pi\ to\n i(/ppon he mounted his horse
X. C. 7.1.1. Extension:

e)pi\ pa=san *)asi/a_n e)llo/gimoi famous over all Asia
P. Criti. 112e.
b. Temporal: extension:

e)pi\ polla\_s h(me/ra_s for many days
D. 21.41.
c. Quantity, measure: e)pi\ mi_kro/n a little, e)pi\ ple/on still more, e)pi\ pa=n in general, pla/tos e)/xwn plei=on h)\ e)pi\ du/o sta/dia wider than (up to) two stades
X. C. 7.5.8.
d. Other relations: Purpose, object in view:

pe/mpein e)pi\ kataskoph/n to send for the purpose of reconnoitering
X. C. 6.2.9,

a)pe/steilan e)pi\ xrh/mata they sent for money
T. 6.74. Hostility: e)/pleon e)pi\ tou\s *)aqhnai/ous they sailed against the Athenians 2. 90. Reference: to\ e)p' e)me/ (with or without ei)=nai) as far as I am concerned (more commonly e)p' e)moi/); to/ ge e)p' e)kei=non ei)=nai
L. 13.58.
N.—To express purpose e)pi/ with accus. is generally used when the purpose involves actual or implied motion to an object; e)pi/ with dat. is used when the purpose may be attained by mental activity.

## 4. e)pi/ in Composition

Upon (e)pigra/fein write upon), over (e)piplei=n sail over), at, of cause (e)pixai/rein rejoice over or at), to, toward (e)pibohqei=n send assistance to), in addition (e)pidido/nai give in addition), against (e)pibouleu/ein plot against), after (e)pigi/gnesqai be born after, e)piskeua/zein repair); causative (e)palhqeu/ein verify); intensity (e)pikru/ptein hide; e)pibouleu/esqai further deliberate = reflect); reciprocity (e)pimei/gnusqai a)llh/lois exchange friendly dealings).

## kata/

§1690

kata/ down (cp. ka/tw), opposed to a)na/. With the genitive (the genitive proper (of the goal) and the ablatival genitive) and the accusative. With the genitive, the motion is perpendicular; with the accusative, horizontal.

## 1. kata/ with the Genitive

a. Local: down from, down toward, under:

a(la/menoi kata\ th=s pe/tra_s having leapt down from the rock
X. A. 4.2.17, kat' a)/kra_s utterly, completely (down from the summit)
P. L. 909b,

yu_xh\ kata\ xqono\s w)/|xeto his soul went down under the earth
*y 100, mu/ron kata\ th=s kefalh=s kataxe/antes having poured myrrh (down) over their heads
P. R. 398a; rarely of rest:

o( kata\ gh=s the man under the earth
X. C. 4.6.5.
b. Temporal (very rare): kata\ panto\s tou= ai)w=nos for all eternity Lyc. 7.
c. Other relations: against, as

kat' e)mautou= e)rei=n to speak against myself
P. A. 37b; rarely in a favourable or neutral sense, as

oi( kata\ *dhmosqe/nous e)/painoi the eulogies on Demosthenes
Aes. 3.50,

kata\ pa/ntwn le/gein to speak with regard to all
X. C. 1.2.16; by (with verbs of swearing), as o)mnu/ntwn to\n o(/rkon kata\ i(erw=n telei/wn let them swear the oath by (lit. down over) fullgrown victims
T. 5.47.

## 2. kata/ with the Accusative

a. Local:

e)/pleon kata\ potamo/n they sailed down-stream
Hdt. 4.44,

kata\ ta\_s ei)so/dous e)fepo/menoi following to the entrances
X. C. 3.3.64. Extension: kaq' o(/lhn th\n po/lin throughout the entire city Lyc. 40,

kata\ gh=n by land
L. 2.32,

diw/kontes tou\s kaq' au(tou/s pursuing those stationed opposite themselves
X. A. 1.10.4.
b. Temporal (post-Homeric):

kata\ plou=n during the voyage
T. 3.32, kat' e)kei=non to\n xro/non at that time 1. 139,

oi( kaq' e(auto/n his contemporaries
D. 20.73.
c. Other relations: Purpose:

kata\ qe/a_n h(=ken came for the purpose of seeing
T. 6.31. Conformity:

kata\ tou/tous r(h/twr an orator after their style
P. A. 17b,

kata\ tou\s no/mous according to the laws
D. 8.2. Ground on which an act is based:

kata\ fili/a_n owing to friendship
T. 1.60. Comparisons: mei/zw h)\ kata\ da/krua peponqo/tes having endured sufferings too great for (than according to) tears 7. 75 (cp. maior quam pro). Manner:

kaq' h(suxi/a_n quietly
T. 6.64. Distribution:

kat' e)/qnh nation by nation
T. 1.122,

de/ka draxmai\ kat' a)/ndra ten drachmae the man
Aes. 3.187,

kata\ sfa=s au)tou/s per se
T. 1.79. Approximate numbers:

kata\ penth/konta about fifty
Hdt. 6.79.

## 3. kata/ in Composition

Down from above (katapi/_ptein fall down), back (katalei/pein leave behind), against, adversely (katagignw/skein condemn, decide against, katafronei=n despise), completely (katapetrou=n stone to death, katesqi/ein eat up), often with an intensive force that cannot be translated. An intransitive verb when compounded with kata/ may become transitive (1559).

## meta/

§1691

meta/: original meaning amid, among (cp. Germ. mit, Eng. mid in midwife). Hence properly only with plurals or collectives (so in Hom. with gen. and dat.). meta/ denotes participation, community of action. peda/ (Lesb. and other dialects) agrees in meaning with meta/, but is of different origin.

## 1. meta/ with the Genitive

Usually of persons and abstract nouns.
Local: among, together with, as

kaqh/menos meta\ tw=n a)/llwn sitting among the rest
P. R. 359e,

qu=sai met' e)kei/nwn to sacrifice in company with them
X. C. 8.3.1; on the side of, as

oi( meta\ *ku/_rou ba/rbaroi the barbarians in the army of Cyrus
X. A. 1.7.10,

meta\ tw=n h)dikhme/nwn polemei=n to wage war on the side of the wronged
D. 9.24,

ou) meta\ tou= plh/qous without the consent of the people
T. 3.66; besides:

geno/menos meta\ tou= cunetou= kai\ dunato/s showing himself powerful as well as sagacious
T. 2.15. Accompanying circumstances (concurrent act or state): meta\kindu/_nwn kthsa/menoi (th\n ta/cin) having acquired their position amid dangers
D. 3.36,

lu/_ph meta\ fo/bou grief and terror
T. 7.75. Joint efficient cause: meta\ po/nwn e)leuqe/ra_n e)poi/hsan th\n *(ella/da by (amid) struggles they freed Greece
L. 2.55. Conformity: meta\ tw=n no/mwn in accordance with the laws 3. 82.

## 2. meta/ with the Dative (Locative）

Chiefly Epic (usually with the plural or with the collective singular of persons or things personified, or of the parts of living objects):

meta\ mnhsth=rsin e)/eipen he spake amid the suitors
r 467,

meta\ fresi/ in their hearts
*d 245.

## 3. meta/ with the Accusative

Local: into the midst of: nekrou\s e)/rusan meta\ la_o\n *)axaiw=n they dragged the dead into the midst of the host of the Achaeans E 573; with an idea of purpose: i)e/nai meta\ *ne/stora to go after (in quest of) Nestor K 73. Extension over the midst of: meta\ plhqu/_n throughout the multitude B 143. Phrase:

meta\ xei=ras e)/xein to have in hand
T. 1.138.
N.—From the use in

met' i)/xnia bai=ne qeoi=o he went after the steps of the goddess
g 30 is derived the prose use: after (of time or rank), as

meta\ ta\ *trwi+ka/ after the Trojan war
T. 2.68, meta\ qeou\s yu_xh\ qeio/taton after the gods the soul is most divine P. L. 726. The range of meta/ with acc. in Attic prose is not wide.

## 4. meta/ in Composition

Among (metadido/nai give a share), after, in quest of (metape/mpesqai send for). When one thing is among other things, it may be said to come after another, to succeed or alternate with it; hence of succession (meqhmerino/s diurnus; cp. meq' h(me/ra_n after daybreak), alteration or change (metagra/fein rewrite, metame/lein repent i.e. care for something else).
When contrasted with su/n, meta/ often denotes participation: o( me/toxos the partner, o( sunw/n the companion. su/n often denotes something added. But meta/ is usually the prose preposition for su/n, though it does not mean inclusive of.

## para/

§1692

para/ (Hom. parai/, Lat. por- in porrigere) alongside, by, near. Except with the accusative para/ is commonly used of persons and personified things.

## 1. para/ with the (Ablatival) Genitive

Usually coming or proceeding from a person, in Hom. also of things; cp. de chez.
a. Local:

oi( au)tomolou=ntes para\ basile/ws the deserters from the king
X. A. 2.1.6. In poetry, where we might expect the dat. (1659 a): e)/greto par' *(/hrhs lit. he awoke from the side of Hera O 5. In standard Attic prose para/ with the gen. of a thing is excessively rare. When so used, the thing is personified, or the thing implies a person (as po/lis, a)rxh/, qe/a_tron).
b. Author, Source (cp. 1410): with verbs of receiving, taking, asking, learning, sending, etc.:

para\ *mh/dwn th\n a)rxh\n e)la/mbanon *pe/rsai the Persians wrested the empire from the Medes
X. A. 3.4.8,

para\ sou= e)ma/qomen we learned from you
X. C. 2.2.6;

h( para\ tw=n qew=n eu)/noia the good-will on the part of the gods
D. 2.1 (less commonly a)po/); with passives and intransitives (instead of u(po/ with the gen. of the agent):

ta\ para\ th=s tu/xhs dwrhqe/nta the gifts of Fortune
I. 4.26, tou=to para\ pa/ntwn o(mologei=tai this is acknowledged on all sides (on the part of all)
L. 30.12.

## 2. para/ with the Dative

Almost always of persons in standard Attic prose; cp. chez.
a. Local:

ou) para\ mhtri\ si_tou=ntai oi' pai=des, a)lla\ para\ tw=| didaska/lw| the boys do not eat with their mothers, but with their teachers
X. C. 1.2.8, par' e)moi/ skhnou=n to mess with me (as chez moi) 6. 1. 49; of things:

ta\ para\ qala/tth xwri/a the places along the sea
X. A. 7.2.25.
b. Other relations: Possessor:

to\ me\n xru_si/on para\ tou/tw|, oi( de\ ki/ndu_noi par' u(_mi=n this man has the gold, you the dangers
Aes. 3.240; of the superior in command:

oi( para\ basilei= o)/ntes those under the king
X. A. 1.5.16; of the person judging:

a)nai/tios para\ toi=s stratiw/tais blameless in the opinion of the troops
X. C. 1.6.10, o(mologei=tai para\ tw=| dh/mw| it is agreed in the opinion of the people Lyc. 54 (here para/ denotes the sphere of judgment); with the gen. after a passive (1692. 1. b) it denotes the source.

## 3. para/ with the Accusative

a. Local: of motion to, in prose only of persons:

h(=ke par' e)me/ come to me
X. C. 4.5.25; motion along, by, past (a place):

para\ gh=n plei=n sail along shore
T. 6.13; of parallel extent (along, alongside, beside) with verbs of motion and of rest (often the dat.), and often when no verb is used:

h(/nper e)/labon nau=n, a)ne/qesan para\ to\ tropai=on the ship they captured they set up alongside of the trophy
T. 2.92,

ei)=pen au)tw=| me/nein par' e(auto/n he told him to remain close by him
X. C. 1.4.18,

to\ pedi/on to\ para\ to\n potamo/n the plain extending along the river
X. A. 4.3.1, h)=n para\ th\n o(do\n krh/nh there was a spring by the road 1. 2. 13. Contrary to: para\ tou\s no/mous h)\ kat' au)tou/s contrary to (i.e. going past) the laws or in accordance with them
D. 23.20; in addition to (along beside):

e)/xw para\ tau=ta a)/llo ti le/gein besides this I have to say something else
P. Ph. 107a. Phrase: par' o)li/gon e)poiou=nto *kle/andron they treated Cleander as of no account (cp. ‘next to nothing’)
X. A. 6.6.11.
b. Temporal: (duration)

para\ pa/nta to\n xro/non throughout the whole time
D. 5.2, (momentary)

para\ ta\ deina/ in the hour of danger
Aes. 3.170, par' au)ta\ ta)_dikh/mata at the time of (i.e. immediately after) the offences themselves
D. 18.13.
c. Other relations: Cause = dia/:

para\ th\n h(mete/ra_n a)me/leian in consequence of our negligence
D. 4.11, ei) para\ to\ proaisqe/sqai kekw/lu_tai if it was prevented by being perceived in advance 19. 42. Dependence: para\ tou=to ge/gone ta\

tw=n *(ellh/nwn the fortunes of the Greeks depend on this
D. 18.232. Measure: para\ mi_kro\n h)/lqomen e)candrapodisqh=nai we had a narrow escape (came by a little) from being enslaved
I. 7.6,

para\ polu/ by far
T. 2.8. Comparison:

e)ce/tason par' a)/llhla contrast with each other
D. 18.265, xeimw\n mei/zwn para\ th\n kaqesthkui=an w(/ra_n stormy weather more severe than was to be expected at the season then present
T. 4.6.

## 4. para/ in Composition

Alongside, by, beside (parie/nai go alongside), beyond, past (parelau/nein drive past), over (parora=n overlook), aside, amiss (parakou/ein misunderstand).

## peri/

§1693

peri/ around (on all sides), about; cp. pe/ric round about. Lat. per in permagnus. peri/ is wider than a)mfi/: cp.
X. Vect. 1.7 ou) peoi/rrutos ou)=sa w(/sper nh=sos . . . a)mfiqa/lattos ga/r e)sti it (Attica) is not, like an island, surrounded by the sea . . . for it has the sea on two sides. On peri/ post-positive, see 1665.

## 1. peri/ with the Genitive

a. Local (poetic): peri\ tro/pios bebaw/s riding on (astride) the keel
e 130.
b. Other relations: about, concerning (Lat. de), the subject about which an act or thought centres:

peri\ patri/dos maxou/menoi fighting for their country
T. 6.69 (cp. u(pe/r),

dei/sa_s peri\ tou= ui(ou= fearing for his son
X. C. 1.4.22,

le/gein peri\ th=s ei)rh/nhs to speak about peace
T. 5.55; ta\ peri/ tinos instead of ta\ peri/ tina is used in the neighbourhood of a verb of saying or thinking (which takes peri/ with gen.):

ta\ peri\ th=s a)reth=s the relations of virtue
P. Pr. 360e. Superiority (cp. 1402):

peri/essi gunaikw=n ei)=dos thou dost surpass women in beauty
s 248, peri\ panto\s poiou/menoi regarding as (more than everything) all-important
T. 2.11 (cp. 1373).

## 2. peri/ with the Dative

a. Local: about: of arms, dress, etc., in prose:

streptoi\ peri\ toi=s traxh/lois collars about their necks
X. A. 1.5.8, a(\ peri\ toi=s sw/masin e)/xousin the clothes about their persons I. ep. 9. 10 (only case in the orators), peri\ douri/ A 303.
b. Other relations (usually poetic): External cause:

dei/santes peri\ tai=s nausi/n afraid for their ships
T. 7.53 (with verbs of fearing, peri/ with the gen. is fear of or fear for). Inner impulse:

peri\ ta/rbei from fear
A. Pers. 694.

## 3. peri/ with the Accusative

a. Local: of position:

a)pe/steilan nau=s peri\ *pelopo/nnhson they despatched ships round about Peloponnese
T. 2.23, w)/|koun peri\ pa=san th\n *sikeli/a_n they settled all round Sicily 6. 2; of persons:

oi( peri\ *(hra(_kleiton the followers of Heraclitus
P. Crat. 440c.
b. Indefinite statement of time and number:

peri\ o)/rqron about dawn
T. 6.101, peri\ e(bdomh/konta about seventy 1. 54.
c. Other relations: Occupation:

oi( peri\ th\n mousikh\n o)/ntes those who are engaged in liberal pursuits
I. 9.4; connected with, of general relation (with reference to):

oi( no/moi oi( peri\ tou\s ga/mous the laws about marriage
P. Cr. 50d,

peri\ qeou\s a)sebe/statoi most impious in regard to the gods
X. H. 2.3.53,

ta\ peri\ ta\_s nau=s naval affairs
T. 1.13. Verbs of action (except verbs of striving) prefer peri/ with accus., verbs of perception, emotion, knowing, prefer peri/ with gen. But the cases often shift.

## 4. peri/ in Composition

Around, about (perie/xein surround), beyond, over (periei=nai excel; and periora=<*> look beyond, overlook, suffer), (remaining) over (perigi/gnesqai remain over, result, and excel), exceedingly (perixarh/s very glad).

## pro/

§1694

pro/ (Lat. pro, for) before. Cp. a)nti/, which is narrower in meaning.

## 1. pro/ with the Genitive only

a. Local:

pro\ tw=n a(macw=n in front of the wagons
X. C. 6.2.36.
b. Temporal:

pro\ th=s ma/xhs before the battle
X. A. 1.7.13.
c. Other relations: Defence or care (cp. u(pe/r): diakindu_neuein pro\ basile/ws to incur danger in defence of (prop. in front of) the king
X. C. 8.8.4. Preference (cp. a)nti/): oi( e)painou=ntes pro\ dikaiosu/nhs a)diki/a_n th<*>se who laud injustice in preference to justice
P. R. 361e, pro\ pollou= poiei=sqai to esteem highly (in preference to much)
I. 5.138, fwnei=n pro\ tw=nde to speak for them (as their spokesman)
S. O. T. 10 (a)nti\ tw=nde = as their deputy, u(pe\r tw=nde as their champion).

## 2. pro/ in Composition

Before, forward, forth (proba/llein put forward), for, in behalf of, in defence of, in public (proagoreu/ein give public notice), beforehand (pro/dhlos manifest beforehand), in preference (proairei=sqai choose in preference).

## pro/s

§1695

pro/s (Hom. also proti/), at, by (fronting). Of like meaning, but of different origin, is Hom. poti/.

## 1. pro/s with the Genitive

a. Local (not common in prose):

to\ pro\s e(spe/ra_s tei=xos the wall facing the west
X. H. 4.4.18,

ta\ u(pozu/gia e)/xontes pro\s tou= potamou= having the pack-animals on the side toward the river
X. A. 2.2.4.
b. Other relations: Descent:

pro\s patro/s on the father's side
Aes. 3.169. Characteristic:

ou) ga\r h)=n pro\s tou= *ku/_rou tro/pou for it was not the way of Cyrus
X. A. 1.2.11. Point of view of a person: pro\s a)nqrw/pwn ai)sxro/s base in the eyes of men 2. 5. 20. Agent as the source, with passive verbs (instead of u(po/): o(mologei=tai pro\s pa/ntwn it is agreed by all 1. 9. 20; to the advantage of;

sponda\_s poihsa/menos pro\s *qhbai/wn ma=llon h)\ pro\s e(aut w=n making a truce more to the advantage of the Thebans than of his own party
X. H. 7.1.17; in oaths and entreaties:

pro\s qew=n by the gods
X. H. 2.4.21.

## 2. pro/s with the Dative

In a local sense, denoting proximity (generally, in prose, of towns or buildings, not of persons):

pro\s th=| po/lei th\n ma/xhn poiei=sqai to fight near the city
T. 6.49; sometimes like e)n, as

pro\s i(eroi=s toi=s koinoi=s a)nateqh=nai to be dedicated in the common shrines
T. 3.57. Occupation:

h)=n o(/los pro\s tw=| lh/mmati he was wholly intent upon his gain
D. 19.127. In addition to:

pro\s au)toi=s besides these
T. 7.57. In the presence of:

pro\s tw=| diaithth= le/gein to speak before the arbitrator
D. 39.22.

## 3. pro/s with the Accusative

a. Local (direction toward or to, strictly fronting, facing):

u(_ma=s a)/comen pro\s au)tou/s we will lead you to them
X. A. 7.6.6, pro\s no/ton (toward the) south
T. 3.6,

i)e/nai pro\s tou\s polemi/ous to go against the enemy
X. A. 2.6.10.
b. Temporal (rare):

pro\s h(me/ra_n toward daybreak
X. H. 2.4.6.
c. Other relations: friendly or hostile relation:

pro\s e)me\ le/gete speak to me
X. C. 6.4.19,

fili/a_ pro\s u(_ma=s friendship with you
I. 5.32,

e)/xqra_ pro\s tou\s *)argei/ous enmity to the Argives
T. 2.68, but h( pro\s h(ma=s e)/xqra_ our enmity 6. 80, h( a)pe/xqeia pro\s tou\s *qhbai/ous our enmity to the Thebans and the enmity of the Thebans to us
D. 18.36. With words of hating, accusing, and their opposites, pro/s is used either of the subject or of the object or of both parties involved. With words denoting warfare pro/s indicates a double relation, and the context must determine which party is the aggressor or assailant:

naumaxi/a_ *korinqi/wn pro\s *kerku_rai/ous a sea-fight between the Corinthians and the Corcyreans
T. 1.13 (here kai/ often suffices, as o( *lakedaimoni/wn kai\ *)hlei/wn po/lemos
X. H. 3.2.31). Relation in general:

ou)de\n au)tw=| pro\s th\n po/lin e)sti/n he has nothing to do with the city
D. 21.44, pro\s tou\s qeou\s eu)sebw=s e)/xein to be pious toward the gods Lyc. 15. Purpose: pro\s ti/; to what end?
X. C. 6.3.20,

pro\s xa/rin le/gein to speak in order to court favour
D. 4.51; with a view to (often nearly = dia/):

pro\s tau=ta bouleu/esqe eu)= wherefore be well advised
T. 4.87, pro\s ta\ paro/nta in consequence of the present circumstances 6. 41. Conformity:

pro\s th\n a)ci/a_n according to merit
X. C. 8.4.29. Standard of judgment:

ou)de\ pro\s a)rgu/rion th\n eu)daimoni/a_n e)/kri_non nor did they estimate happiness by the money-standard
I. 4.76, xw/ra_ w(s pro\s to\ plh=qos tw=n poli_tw=n e)laxi/sth a territory very small in proportion to the number of its citizens 4. 107; and hence of comparison:

oi/ faulo/teroi tw=n a)nqrw/pwn pro\s tou\s cunetwte/rous . . . a)/meinon oi)kou=si ta\_s po/leis the simpler class of men, in comparison with the more astute, manage their public affairs better
T. 3.37. Exchange:

h(dona\_s pro\s h(dona\_s katalla/ttesqai to exchange pleasures for pleasures
P. Ph. 69a.

## 4. pro/s in Composition

To, toward (proselau/nein drive to, prostre/pein turn toward), in addition (proslamba/nein take in addition), against (proskrou/ein strike against, be angry with). Often in the general sense of additionally, qualifying the whole sentence rather than the verb.

## su/n

§1696

su/n (Older Attic cu/n; cp. Ion. cu_no/s from konios = koino/s, Lat. cum) with.

## 1. su/n with the Instrumental Dative only.

a. In standard (i.e. not Xenophontic) prose su/n has been almost driven out of use by meta/. It is used (1) in old formulas, as su\n (toi=s) qeoi=s with the help of the gods, su\n (toi=s) o(/plois in arms, etc. (of things attached to a person), su\n nw=| intelligently; (2) of sum totals (along with, including), as

su\n toi=s e)/rgois ple/on h)\ de/ka ta/lanta e)/xei he has more than ten talents interest included
D. 28.13.
b. su/n is usually poetic (rare in comedy) and Xenophontic; it is often used in the formulas of a (1) and of persons and things personified. Its older and poetic meaning is along with (of something secondary or added to the action) and with the help of. So in Xen.: together with, along with:

su\n th= gunaiki\ deipnei=n to sup with your wife
X. C. 6.1.49; to reinforce the simple dative: a)kolouqei=n su/n tini, poreu/esqai su/n tini (1524); with the collateral notion of help: with the aid of, as

su\n e)kei/nw| ma/xesqai to fight with his help
X. C. 5.3.5.
c. Means and Instrument (regarded as accompaniments of an action: the comitative instrumental): h( kth=sis au)tw=n e)/stin ou)damw=s su\n th=| bi/a|, a)lla\ ma=llon su\n th=| eu)ergesi/a| they (friends) are acquired, not by forcible means, but by kindness
X. C. 8.7.13.
d. Manner:

su\n ge/lwti h)=lqon they went laughing
X. A. 1.2.18. In conformity with (opp. to para/): ou)k e)pe/treye tw=| dh/mw| para\ tou\s no/mous yhfi/sasqai, a)lla\ su\n toi=s no/mois h)nantiw/qh ktl. he did not permit the people to vote contrary to the laws, but, in conformity with them, opposed himself, etc.
X. M. 4.4.2.

## 2. su/n in Composition

Together with (sumbiou=n live with, sumporeu/esqai march in company with), together (sumba/llein conicere), completely (sumplhrou=n fill up), contraction in size (sunte/mnein cut short), and generally of union or connection. Standard prose uses sun- freely.

## u(pe/r
